area: First-time teacher, cold start to printable sheets: sign in, find the class, add students, build an MCQ exam with real questions and answer key, generate OMR sheets, get something printable
worked: The 3-step create wizard, the Review screen (answer key shown green with a "Correct: B" line per question), and the print packet are genuinely good: clicking Generate sheets produced a correct 10-page PDF in ~1.5s with per-student names, QR, corner fiducials, and the packet PDF interleaves a per-student shuffled question paper with that student's sheet, which is exactly what a teacher needs to hand out.

findings.title: No bulk student entry anywhere: 4 interactions per student and the modal closes after every single one
findings.route: /classes/<id>/students (also reached by the class overview "Add students" button, which just lands on the same page)
findings.observed: The only way to add a student is the "Add student" button, which opens a modal with Full name / Roll number / Section. I timed it: 5 students cost exactly 20 interactions (open modal, type name, type roll, click Add) because the modal CLOSES after each save, forcing you to re-click "Add student" every time. I searched every class-scoped route (/overview, /students, /settings, /subjects, /exams, /access) for the words import, csv, upload, paste, bulk, excel: zero hits (the only "bulk" match was a seeded student literally named "Bulk Test 1"). The orphan /rosters/<id> detail page also offers only "Add student" singular, no paste box.
findings.why_it_hurts: A school teacher with 40 students per class spends ~160 modal interactions per class and ~960 across 6 classes before they can print anything. The coaching institute owner with 300 students faces ~1200. Every school already has this list in a spreadsheet. This is the single thing that makes a real teacher close the tab and go back to photocopying a blank OMR sheet.
findings.fix: Add a "Add many students" button next to "Add student" opening a textarea that accepts pasted lines ("101, Asha Rao" / tab-separated from Excel) plus a CSV file drop, with a preview table showing parsed roll+name and duplicate-roll warnings before commit. As a minimum stopgap, keep the existing modal open after save, clear the fields, auto-increment the roll number, and focus the name field, which alone takes it from 4 interactions per student to 2.

findings.title: Question text is mandatory, so there is no way to make a bubble sheet from an answer key you already have
findings.observed: I filled in Option A, Option B and picked the correct answer but left the question stem empty: "Save question" stayed disabled. It only enabled once I typed stem text. There is no "answer key only" mode, no "how many questions / how many options" setup field, and no import of a key like "1-B 2-C 3-A".
findings.why_it_hurts: The overwhelmingly common OMR case is a teacher who ALREADY has the question paper in Word or as a photocopy and only needs the bubble sheet plus the key. This app forces them to retype 20 stems and 80 option texts they already have. I measured a 10-question exam at 103 interactions; 20 questions is ~205. That is 20 to 40 minutes of typing to produce a sheet they wanted in two minutes.
findings.fix: Add a third "Test mode" on step 1 called "Answer key only (I have my own question paper)" which asks for number of questions and options per question, then shows a compact key grid where the teacher clicks A/B/C/D per row. Make question text optional in that mode and label the sheet rows by number only. Also accept a pasted key string.

findings.title: Question builder starts at 2 options and never collapses: 10 questions costs 103 clicks and a 5411px page
findings.observed: Every new question card starts with only Option A and Option B, so for a normal 4-option MCQ you click "+ Add option" twice per question, every question, forever. There is no "options per question" default. Saved questions stay fully expanded as editable forms rather than collapsing to a one-line summary: I measured the page at 5411px with 10 questions saved (~490px each), so a 20-question test is roughly a 10,800px scroll with no question index, no jump-to-question, no collapse-all, and no sticky Next button. Per question the cost is: type stem, +Add option x2, type 4 options, click the correct radio, click "Save question", click "+ Add question" = 10 interactions.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the bulk of the teacher's time. 5 questions cost me 49 interactions; 20 questions costs ~205. And once you are 15 questions deep you cannot see or verify the key you set for question 3 without scrolling thousands of pixels.
findings.fix: Default new questions to 4 options with a class-level or exam-level "options per question" setting on step 1. Collapse a saved question to a single row reading "3. Which of these is a noble gas? Answer: B" with an edit affordance. Add a sticky question-number rail for jumping, and make Enter in the last option field save and open the next question so a full test can be typed without touching the mouse.

findings.title: The printed sheet's Roll No. grid has only 2 digit columns while the app prints 3-digit roll numbers on the same page
findings.observed: The roster and the student picker show roll numbers as 001, 002 ... 010, 771, 901. The generated question paper header prints "Roll No.: 006". But the answer sheet's bubble grid on the very same student's page has exactly two digit columns, headed 0 and 1. A student told to bubble 006 physically cannot.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is a trust breaker at the moment of truth. Either the student bubbles something wrong and the scan mis-identifies them, or the invigilator has to give verbal instructions contradicting what is printed on the paper. For the coaching institute with 300 students the grid would need 3 columns and the app is silently deriving column count from the integer value of the selected students' rolls, so two batches of the same test get different sheet layouts.
findings.fix: Size the roll grid from the widest roll-number STRING in the selected roster (not the parsed integer), so "006" gets 3 columns with a leading zero column. Show the digit count on the Generate page ("Roll No. grid: 3 digits") so the teacher can see it before printing 40 sheets.

findings.title: After "Finish & mark ready" you are dumped on the class overview, where exam rows are not clickable and the button just says "Generate"
findings.route: Click "Finish & mark ready" on step 3, land on /classes/<id>
findings.observed:
Finishing the wizard navigates to the class overview and shows a toast "Test marked as ready!". The "Recent exams" widget there lists my exam, but I checked the DOM: the title is a plain

inside

  • with cursor:auto, and clicking it does nothing. The only control is a button labelled "Generate" (generate what?). The widget shows no status badge, no date, no question count, so my one READY exam sat among four identically-named DRAFTs left over from abandoned wizard runs with nothing to tell them apart. Meanwhile the best page in the whole app, /tests/, which shows QUESTIONS 5 / TOTAL MARKS 5 / MODE Standard and a "Lifecycle" card grid of Edit questions, Generate & print, Scan sheets, Results, Analytics, is never shown to you and is only reachable via the small "View all" link then clicking a title in the table.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the exact moment the teacher asks "what now?". They are shown a list they cannot click, a verb with no object, and no confirmation of what they just built. The orientation page that would answer the question exists and is excellent, and the flow routes around it.
findings.fix: On finish, navigate to /tests/<id> and show the Lifecycle hub with step 2 "Generate & print" visually next. Make the Recent exams rows links to /tests/<id>, add the READY/DRAFT badge and question count that the Exams table already has, and rename the row button to "Generate sheets" to match.

findings.title: The print buttons appear below the fold after you click Generate, and the toast covers where they land
findings.observed: On a 1440x900 viewport I clicked "Generate sheets" (which sits at y~890, right at the bottom edge). The success panel with "Open & print", "Download sheets PDF" and "Download print packet" renders at y~996 in a 1079px document, entirely below the fold. scrollY after generating was 13, so the page does not scroll to it. The only on-screen change is a transient bottom-right toast reading "Generated 10 sheet(s)", which sits over the same corner of the screen. To a teacher the page looks unchanged.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher clicks the big button, sees a toast flash, and concludes nothing happened, or clicks Generate a second time. The entire point of the visit, getting a printable, is one scroll away and invisible.
findings.fix: Scroll the success panel into view and focus it after generation, or better, put the print actions in a sticky footer bar that appears in place of the Generate button. State the result concretely: "10 sheets ready, 10 pages".

findings.title: On mobile every switch and checkbox is stretched into an unreadable blob by a height-only tap-target fix
findings.observed: I measured the controls at 320px: the shuffle and branding switches are 32px wide by 40px tall, and the per-student checkboxes are 16px wide by 40px tall. The 40px minimum tap height is being applied without matching width, so a 32x18 pill switch renders as a tall rounded blob with a circular thumb floating in it, and you cannot tell whether "Use organisation logo and heading", "Shuffle questions" and "Shuffle options" are on or off. Checkboxes render as thin vertical bars. The page H1 is also truncated to "Generate O…".
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the phone screen where a teacher decides which students get sheets and whether questions get shuffled, and the on/off state is unreadable. Shuffle being silently wrong is a grading-integrity issue, not cosmetic. (Positive note: I found no horizontal overflow at 320px on any journey page, and the Exams table degrades cleanly to stacked cards.)
findings.fix: Give the switch and checkbox a transparent tap-target wrapper (min-height 40px, min-width 40px) instead of stretching the control itself, so the visible pill stays 32x18 and the square stays 16x16 centred inside it. Let the H1 wrap rather than truncate.

findings.title: Abandoned wizard runs become permanent DRAFT exams with identical names and there is no delete or rename anywhere
findings.observed: Every time I entered the wizard and left before finishing, a DRAFT exam was persisted. I ended with five rows all titled "Unit Test 3 Chemistry", all dated Jul 27 2026, one READY and four DRAFT. I opened the "More test actions" menu: it contains Scan, Results, Review, Analytics, Retest. No Delete, no Rename, no Duplicate. I searched /tests/<id>, /tests/<id>/questions and class settings for delete/archive/duplicate/rename: only class settings has a delete (for the class). Nothing warns about the duplicate title.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who gets called away mid-exam-build permanently pollutes their list, and after a term the Exams page is unusable junk they cannot clean. Worse, the DRAFT rows still show an enabled "Generate sheets" button, so it is easy to print sheets for the wrong copy. "Duplicate this test for another section" is also the single most-wanted action for a teacher with 6 classes and it is missing.
findings.fix: Add Rename, Duplicate and Delete to the row menu with a custom confirm modal. Do not persist a test until the title step is submitted, or auto-clean untitled drafts. Warn on a duplicate title within the same class.

findings.title: The printed sheet uses under a third of the A4 page, with ~3.8mm bubbles crammed into the top-left corner and no student instructions
findings.route: The generated PDF from Open & print
findings.observed: On the A4 page the header, the roll grid and the five answer rows all sit in roughly the top-left quarter; measuring against the page width, the answer bubbles are about 3.5 to 4mm across and the whole answer block occupies about a 25mm by 95mm strip, leaving well over 70 percent of the sheet blank. The sheet carries no instructions at all: no "use HB pencil", no "fill the bubble completely", no "do not fold or staple", no marks per question, and the question paper page carries no total marks, duration, or negative-marking note even though the teacher configured a marking scheme.
findings.why_it_hurts: The stated workflow is a teacher photographing sheets with a phone. Small, tightly packed bubbles in one corner of a mostly-empty page is the worst case for phone-camera detection and will push avoidable reads into the review queue, which is the thing that destroys trust in auto-grading. And students who tick or cross instead of filling will be marked wrong through no fault of their own because nothing told them how to mark.
findings.fix: Scale the bubble grid to fill the printable area (target 5 to 6mm bubbles) and flow into 2 or 3 columns as question count grows. Print a short instruction block and the marking scheme the teacher already configured ("1 mark each, no negative marking") on both the question paper and the sheet.

findings.title: The icon-only sidebar hides the app's entire mental model behind mouse hover
findings.observed: The left rail shows 7 to 9 unlabelled 39x36 icons. Only on mouse hover does it fly out to reveal labels, and inside an exam those labels are a numbered pipeline: Overview, Build 1, Generate 2, Scan 3, Review 4, Results 5, Analytics 6. That numbered pipeline is exactly the explanation a first-time teacher needs and it is invisible unless you happen to hover. Separately, at organisation level the flyout contains only All organizations, Dashboard, Members, Roles & permissions, Usage, Billing and Settings, with no Exams and no Students entry at all.
findings.why_it_hurts: A hover-only affordance does not exist on a tablet or phone, and a first-time user does not hover over a rail of grey glyphs. The teacher's whole job (make an exam, print it, scan it) is fronted by an admin-flavoured nav, while the one nav that would teach them the workflow is hidden.
findings.fix: Ship the sidebar expanded with labels by default on desktop and let the user collapse it, persisting the choice. On the exam pages render the numbered steps as a visible horizontal stepper at the top of the content area so the pipeline is legible on every device.

findings.title: An entire orphan "Rosters" section exists, unreachable from any navigation, holding two rosters both named "Students"
findings.route: /rosters and /rosters/<id> (typed by hand; no link to it exists in the class, exam or organisation nav)
findings.observed: The Generate page's roster dropdown is labelled "Roster", a term that appears nowhere else in the flow. Hunting for it I found /rosters: a real, working page titled "Rosters, Manage student rosters for OMR sheet generation" listing "Grade 10 roster (10)", "Students (4)" and "Students (5)". The sidebar on that page is completely empty apart from the logo. The two rosters auto-created for the classes I made are both literally named "Students" and are indistinguishable. /folders is a second orphan page in the same state ("Folders, Group your classes and share them with your team", one folder "JEE 2026 Batches"). Typing /rosters/new produced "Couldn't load roster, Something went wrong while loading this roster" with 404 and 500 console errors, though the "Create roster" button on /rosters correctly opens a modal instead.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher hits the word "Roster" at the single most consequential moment, choosing who gets a printed sheet, with no way to find out what a roster is or how it relates to the class and section they already set up. When two rosters are both called "Students", picking the wrong one prints sheets for the wrong children. Whole shipped features being reachable only by URL guessing is also the clearest sign of an unfinished information architecture.
findings.fix: Either link Rosters and Folders from the class and organisation nav, or drop the word "Roster" from the Generate page and label that control "Who gets a sheet" with class and section options. Auto-created rosters must inherit the class and section name ("Grade 10 / Section A"), never "Students".

findings.title: Five words for three things: exam, test, roster, section, attempt, lifecycle, retest
findings.observed: On one screen the button says "New exam", the destination H1 says "Create test", the URL is /tests/new, the section heading says "Recent exams", and the success toast says "Test marked as ready!". The sidebar says "Exams", the row menu says "Retest", the exam page calls its card grid "Lifecycle", every exam row is tagged "attempt #1", the Generate page introduces "Roster", and the class page has "Sections" whose cards read "Section A / Section". The hidden native select behind the section picker even says "Whole class (all groups)" while the visible control says "Whole class (all sections)".
findings.why_it_hurts: A first-time teacher genuinely cannot tell whether a test and an exam are two different objects, whether a roster is a class or a section, or what "attempt #1" and "Retest" mean. Every one of those pauses costs seconds and confidence, and the section-versus-roster ambiguity has real consequences because it decides who gets printed sheets.
findings.fix: Pick one user-facing noun (Exam) and use it in every label, heading, toast and URL. Replace "Lifecycle" with "Next steps", "attempt #1" with nothing (or "Attempt 1 of 1" only when a retest exists), and "Retest" with "Create a retest". Drop "Roster" in favour of class and section.

findings.title: Step 1 forces eight marking-policy decisions and 1200px of scroll before you can type a single question
findings.observed: Before reaching "Next: Add questions" the teacher scrolls a ~1200px form covering Title, Section, Subject, Test mode (Standard vs Roster pre-bubbled roll numbers), Marks per correct, Negative marks per wrong, Partial marking, Multiple correct answers allowed, a four-option "If a student marks too many bubbles" policy (Flag for review / Disqualify / Mark wrong / Correct if key marked), and Sheet branding. Only the Title is required. There is no exam date field, no duration, and no total-marks preview anywhere.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher between periods wants Title then Next. Instead they are asked to adjudicate overmarking policy for a test they have not written yet, and the two things they would actually record (date and duration) are absent, so with six classes a week the Exams list has nothing but identical "Jul 27, 2026" created stamps to distinguish rows.
findings.fix: Show Title, Section and Subject, with everything else folded into a collapsed "Marking and sheet options (defaults are fine)" disclosure. Add an exam date field and surface it as a column on the Exams table.

findings.title: Review step reviews only the questions, never the settings, and sheet branding is asked twice with a separate save button
findings.observed: Step 3 lists the questions with the correct option in green and a "Correct: B" line, which is good, but it shows nothing about the marking scheme, negative marking, overmark policy, section or mode chosen on step 1, and no "5 questions, 5 total marks" summary. Separately, "Use organisation logo and heading" is asked once on step 1 as "Sheet branding (optional)" and again on the Generate page as "Sheet heading & logo", where it has its own "Save branding" button and the caption "Save changes before generating".
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who mistyped negative marking as 1 instead of 0.25 will never catch it, and will only find out when scores come back wrong, which is precisely the kind of thing that destroys confidence in an auto-grader. The duplicated branding control with a manual save is a trap: toggle it, click Generate, and your change is silently not applied.
findings.fix: Put a settings summary card at the top of step 3 ("5 questions, 5 marks, 1 mark each, no negative marking, overmarked questions go to review, Whole class, Standard mode") with an Edit link back to step 1. Ask for branding once, and auto-save it on toggle so no separate Save button is needed.

findings.title: The student picker is a fixed-height inner scroller with no search, and the file you download is misnamed
findings.observed: The Students list is a ~230px inner scrollbox showing 6 of 10 students on desktop and about 4 on mobile, nested inside a page that also scrolls. There is no search box and no section filter inside it, though "Clear all" does correctly flip to "Select all" and the Generate button correctly disables at 0 selected. Separately, the button labelled "Download print packet (questions + sheets)" saves a file named question-papers.pdf, though I verified the file does contain 20 pages, both papers and sheets.
findings.why_it_hurts: With 40 students, deselecting the three who were absent means scroll-hunting inside a small box nested in a scrolling page. The misnamed download means a teacher who saves both files ends up unsure which one has the bubble sheets in it, minutes before a print run.
findings.fix: Let the student list grow to its natural height (or at least ~50vh) and add a search field plus section chips above it. Name the downloads after the exam: "Unit Test 3 Chemistry - answer sheets.pdf" and "Unit Test 3 Chemistry - print packet.pdf".

findings.title: Small trust and polish leaks: marketing 404 for signed-in users, "frontend" browser tab title, dead stat tiles
findings.route: any bad in-app URL; every page; /classes/<id>
findings.observed: Hitting a wrong in-app path while signed in (I tried /tests/<id>/build) renders the PUBLIC marketing site: "DoxaEd OMR, Features, Pricing, Sign in, Get started, Start free" with a 404. The browser tab title is the literal string "frontend" on every page of the app. And on the class overview the four stat tiles (EXAMS 6, STUDENTS 10, SECTIONS 1, SUBJECTS 0) are non-interactive divs, confirmed cursor:auto, even though they are the most obvious thing to click to drill in.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who follows a stale bookmark is shown a page inviting them to sign in and start free, which reads as being logged out and losing their work. Six identical "frontend" tabs makes juggling classes impossible. Clicking a big number that does nothing is a small dead end that teaches users the interface is not responsive to them.
findings.fix: Render an in-app 404 inside the signed-in shell with a link back to the class. Set a per-route document title ("Unit Test 3 Chemistry, Generate, DoxaEd OMR"). Make the stat tiles links to /exams, /students, and the sections and subjects pages.

area: Organization side: settings, members, roles and permissions, usage, billing, folders, multi-class/multi-section structure, running one exam across sections, bulk throughput, and cross-test ranking (coaching institute owner, 300 students, 4 staff)
worked: Every destructive action on the org surface (Remove member, Delete class, Delete organization) uses a properly styled custom modal with type-the-org-name confirmation on delete, no native alert/confirm/prompt fired anywhere in the whole audit, no gradients, no horizontal overflow down to 320px, and the 1600px content cap is honoured at 2200px wide.

findings.title: Every invited staff member silently gets org-wide visibility of all 300 students' results; the invite dialog has no scope field
findings.observed: The Invite member modal collects only Email + Role. Its helper text reads "Sets what they can do org-wide. You can scope them to specific classes later." On acceptance the server runs RoleBinding.objects.create(role=invitation.rbac_role, scope_group=None) — an org-wide binding. common/scope.py resolves visibility as the UNION of RoleBindings and per-class PermissionGrants, so a Teacher invited this way sees every class, every exam and every student's marks in the whole institute from the moment they log in. The Members table shows only Email / Role / Status — it never displays a member's effective scope, so nothing on screen tells the owner that staff member #2 can read staff member #3's batch results. Narrowing later requires going to Roles & permissions → Member roles and DELETING the org-wide binding (the "x"), not just adding a scoped one — add a scoped binding and the union still yields org-wide. The UI never says this.
findings.why_it_hurts: The single reason an institute owner pays for a multi-staff product is that the Physics tutor must not see the Chemistry batch's marks or the topper list. This ships default-open, silently, with the remedy hidden two pages away and the union semantics undocumented. An owner will hand out 4 invites believing "Teacher" is a restricted role and only discover otherwise when a tutor quotes another batch's scores.
findings.fix: Add a required Scope selector to the Invite member dialog (default: "No classes yet — grant access per class"), create the RoleBinding with that scope_group on accept, and add an "Access" column to the Members table showing the resolved scope ("Whole organization" / "Grade 10 + sections" / "3 classes"). When Member roles already holds an org-wide binding for a user, block or warn on adding a narrower one: "This member already has org-wide access. Remove it first, otherwise the wider grant still applies."

findings.title: No bulk student import anywhere: 300 students means ~1200 interactions, one modal at a time
findings.observed: I timed it. The Add student modal takes Full name + Roll number + Section, and it CLOSES on every successful add. Adding 3 students cost 12 interactions and 6.8 seconds of pure mechanics (open modal, type name, type roll, submit, modal closes, reopen). There is no CSV upload, no paste-a-list textarea, no "add another" checkbox, no roll-number auto-increment, and no import on the roster detail page either (its only actions are "Add student" and "Add blank sheets"). The class Students list rows are also inert — clicking "Asha Rao" does nothing, so there is no edit, no delete, no move-between-sections, and no multi-select.
findings.why_it_hurts: A coaching institute onboards 300 students at once and churns 20 a month. At 4 interactions per student that is roughly 1200 clicks and keystrokes of modal ping-pong before the product does anything useful. The institute already has the roster in a spreadsheet from admissions. This is the single thing that makes an owner close the tab on day one.
findings.fix: Add "Import students" to the class Students page and the roster page: a paste box accepting "Roll, Name" lines plus a CSV drop zone, with a preview table, per-row error flags and a section assignment for the whole batch. Short term, keep the Add student modal open after submit, auto-increment the roll number, and keep focus on the name field so at least rapid manual entry is 2 keystrokes per student.

findings.title: On a phone, every organization admin page is unreachable by navigation
findings.observed: At 390px the hamburger drawer is built from a hardcoded NAV list (components/shell/nav-config.js) containing exactly two entries: "Classes" and "Settings" (which points at /profile). The org-scoped panel resolved in AppShell.usePanel is never fed to the drawer. The bottom tab bar has Classes / Organizations / Account. On the org home at 390px the only visible controls I could enumerate were: New class, the Grade 10 card, and the three bottom tabs. Result: Members, Roles & permissions, Usage, Billing, Organization settings and Audit log have zero mobile entry points. Typing /org/doxaed-demo/billing directly renders fine — the pages are responsive, they are just unreachable.
findings.why_it_hurts: An institute owner is not at a desk. Approving a new tutor, checking whether the scan quota is about to run out mid-test-day, or upgrading the plan are exactly the things done from a phone between batches. Right now the answer is "find a laptop or type a URL from memory".
findings.fix: Feed the runtime-resolved panel (usePanel) into MobileDrawer instead of the static NAV constant, so the drawer shows the same Dashboard / Members / Roles / Usage / Billing / Settings list the desktop rail shows. As a minimum, add an "Organization" section to the drawer and an org-admin card row to the mobile org home.

findings.title: Students added to a class never reach the roster the Generate page prints from, and it fails silently
findings.observed: Each group (class or section) keeps its own hidden roster. I added three students via the class Students page with the Section dropdown at its default ("Section A"); the class header updated to 13 students. I then opened Generate for the whole-class exam "Midterm Physics": the roster picker defaulted to "Grade 10", the student list showed "10 of 10 selected", and Bulk Test 1/2/3 were absent. The roster dropdown offers "Grade 10" and "Grade 10 · Section A" as separate single-select entries; there is no "everyone in this class" roster and no way to select two rosters at once. So the 10 originally seeded students (direct on the class) and the 3 section students can never be printed in the same run.
findings.why_it_hurts: There is no warning, no count mismatch, no "3 students in this class are not on any selected roster". The owner prints what looks like a full set, walks into the hall, and three students have no sheet. That is the failure that destroys trust in the whole product, and it is invisible until exam morning.
findings.fix: On the Generate page, replace the single roster Select with a class-scoped student picker grouped by section (checkbox per section header, "Select all" at the top), and always reconcile against the class roll: show a persistent banner "13 students in Grade 10, 10 selected — 3 not covered" with a one-click fix. If rosters must stay the unit, at least allow multi-select and show the union count.

findings.title: Running one exam across sections costs a separate generate run and PDF per section, and the results can never be compared by section
findings.observed: The test wizard correctly offers "Whole class (all sections)", so the exam object spans sections. But Generate is single-roster: for 4 batches you run Generate four times, get four separate PDFs, and burn four of the Free plan's 5 daily generations. On the way back out, /tests/:id/results has columns Roll, Name, Score, Correct/Wrong/Blank, Flag, Details — no Section column, no rank, no sorting. Analytics has Overview / Questions / Item Analysis / Improvement and no section filter or section breakdown anywhere (grep of Results.jsx and Analytics.jsx confirms no section handling).
findings.why_it_hurts: "Same test, all batches, then compare batches" is the core weekly ritual of a coaching institute and the reason it runs one exam instead of four. The product supports the setup and then drops the payoff: you cannot answer "did Batch B underperform Batch A on Thursday's test", and printing is N manual cycles instead of one.
findings.fix: Let Generate produce sheets for multiple sections in one action (one job, optionally one PDF with section separator pages, one quota unit). Add a Section column plus a section filter to the Results table, and a "By section" comparison card to Analytics Overview (mean, median, count per section).

findings.title: An existing class can never be moved into a folder, and the folder's own empty state tells you to do exactly that
findings.observed: FolderDetail's empty state reads: "Create a class here, or move an existing class into this folder from its edit screen." I went to the class edit screen. /classes/:id/settings contains exactly three things: Name, Description (optional), Save changes, and a Delete class danger zone. There is no folder field. Grepping confirms the folder picker exists only in NewClass.jsx ("Folder (optional)", applied at creation) and there is no move action on FolderDetail either.
findings.why_it_hurts: An institute arrives with 12 existing batches and wants to group them (JEE / NEET / Foundation) so it can share a whole group with one tutor in one action. Folders can only ever hold classes created after the folder existed, so the feature is useless for every account that already has data, and the app confidently sends the user to a screen that does not have the control.
findings.fix: Add a Folder select to /classes/:id/settings, and a "Move classes into this folder" multi-select picker on FolderDetail. Until then, fix the empty-state copy so it does not send users on a hunt for a control that does not exist.

findings.title: Folders and Rosters have no navigation entry anywhere and render with a completely empty sidebar
findings.observed: I enumerated every clickable element in the left rail on each route. On /org/doxaed-demo the rail has Dashboard, Members, Roles & permissions, Usage, Billing, Settings. On a class it has Overview, Exams, Students, Subjects, Teacher access, Settings. Neither list contains Folders or Rosters, and Cmd-K's "Go to" group offers only Classes, Profile, Organizations. On /folders and /folders/:id the rail collapses to three items total: "Skip to main content", the DX logo, and the account avatar — usePanel returns null for these paths so there is no panel and no rail. Once inside a folder there is no link back to the folder list.
findings.why_it_hurts: Folders are pitched on the page itself as "Group your classes and share them with your team" — the exact multi-staff organising tool an institute owner is looking for — and the only way to reach it is to already know the URL. Rosters, which are what sheet generation actually prints from, are equally invisible. A whole feature area is dark.
findings.fix: Add Folders and Rosters to the org rail (and to Cmd-K "Go to"), and give /folders, /folders/:id, /rosters, /rosters/:id a resolved panel in usePanel so the rail is populated and folder detail has a "Back to folders" link.

findings.title: System roles open in a full editor with editable name and checkboxes that always rejects the save; all six shipped roles are system roles
findings.observed: Every card is badged SYSTEM (Admin 19, Office 8, Owner 20, Supervisor 15, Teacher 13, Viewer 2 permissions). Clicking "View permissions" opens a dialog titled "Edit role, Office" with an editable Name input, 20 live checkboxes grouped Organization / Structure / Exams, and a primary "Save role" button. I unchecked a permission and clicked Save: toast "System roles can't be edited." Nothing is disabled, greyed, or marked read-only beforehand.
findings.why_it_hurts: An owner's very first customisation instinct is "Teacher should not be able to delete groups". The UI lets them think through and toggle a dozen permissions, then throws it away. Since 100% of the roles an account starts with are system roles, 100% of first attempts to tune permissions end in a rejected save. The only escape (New role, build 20 checkboxes from scratch) is not signposted.
findings.fix: When the role is a system role, render the dialog read-only: disable the name input and checkboxes, drop "Save role", and put a "Duplicate as custom role" primary button in its place that pre-fills a new role with these permissions.

findings.title: No ranking or comparison across tests exists, and no student has a page outside a single test
findings.observed: Every ranking surface is single-test: Analytics "Top performers", the published public leaderboard, and StudentDetail's Rank/Percentile (which takes testId + studentId and links only "Back to results"). There is no route or view listing a student's scores across their test history, no class-level or org-level leaderboard, and no cross-test comparison. "Improvement" is not it either — it only compares retest attempts of one test's chain. Meanwhile /built-for advertises "Batch whole cohorts and rank them across every test" and /pricing-adjacent copy says "rank students with item analysis across tests".
findings.why_it_hurts: Weekly tests exist so an institute can publish a running cumulative rank and spot who is sliding. Right now the owner would have to export CSVs from each week's Analytics and rebuild the ranking in Excel — which is what they were paying to stop doing. The marketing pages promise the feature the product does not have, which is worse than silence.
findings.fix: Add a class-level Leaderboard view aggregating the last N tests (cumulative and average percentage, rank, rank delta vs previous test) and a per-student page reachable from the class Students list showing every test that student sat with score, percentile and trend. Until it ships, remove the cross-test ranking claims from the marketing pages.

findings.title: The seat cap is only revealed after composing an invite, and the error toast offers no way to upgrade
findings.route: /org/doxaed-demo/members → Invite member → fill email → Send invitation
findings.observed: The demo org is on Free: 1 seat, and Usage shows "Members (seats) 1 / 1 · 100% of your quota" with a full red bar. The Members page itself shows no seat count at all (just "Doxaed Demo School · 1 member"), and the "Invite member" button is fully enabled. I filled in staff1@doxaed.com, chose Teacher, hit Send invitation and got a bottom-right toast: "Seat limit reached for your plan. Upgrade to add more staff." with no link, no button, and no plan comparison. The modal stayed open with the data still in it and no inline error.
findings.why_it_hurts: The owner does the work, then hits a wall, then has to go hunting for Billing themselves. Worse, at 1 seat the multi-staff half of the product — the reason an institute is evaluating it — cannot be tried at all, so nobody can validate that staff isolation works before paying.
findings.fix: Show "1 of 1 seats used" next to the Members heading; when seats are exhausted, disable Invite member with that reason on hover and surface an inline "Upgrade to add seats" link, and give the failure toast an "Upgrade" action that routes to /org/:slug/billing. Consider making the Free plan 2 seats so isolation is testable.

findings.title: The Analytics "Improvement" tab renders a completely blank page with no message
findings.observed: Clicking Improvement leaves the tab bar with an entirely empty body below it — no chart, no empty state, no loading text, nothing. The API is fine: GET /analytics/test/:id/improvement/ returns 200 with {"chain":[{...one entry...}],"students":{},"class_average":{},"trend":"insufficient_data"}. In Analytics.jsx the guard is `hasChain = chain.length > 0 || Object.keys(classAverage).length > 0`, which is true for a single-attempt test, so the "No retest chain" EmptyState is skipped and lineData comes out empty. The returned trend:"insufficient_data" is ignored entirely. The other three tabs all degrade correctly ("No question difficulty data available", "Item analysis unavailable").
findings.why_it_hurts: A blank screen reads as a broken product, not as "no data yet". The owner clicks the one tab named after the thing they care about across weekly tests and gets nothing to act on and no hint that a Retest is what would populate it — especially since Retest is buried in a 28px kebab on the exams table.
findings.fix: Treat chain.length < 2 (or trend === "insufficient_data") as empty and render the existing EmptyState with a direct "Create a retest" action button, rather than falling through to an empty chart.

findings.title: Two overlapping staff-isolation mechanisms with no explanation of how they combine
findings.observed: Isolation is configured in two unconnected places. Roles & permissions → Member roles → Assign role offers Member / Role / Scope where Scope is "Whole organization" or a top-level class ("Grade 10 (+ its sub-groups)"). Separately, each class has a Teacher access page: "Grant teachers access to this class... Teachers without a grant can't see this class; admins always have full access." The Members page points only at the first ("Scope someone to specific classes in Roles & permissions → Member roles"), the Teacher access page never mentions the first, and neither says whether a teacher needs one, the other, or both. In the backend they are OR'd (RoleBinding ∪ PermissionGrant in common/scope.py) — the more permissive wins.
findings.why_it_hurts: An owner locking down 4 staff cannot form a mental model of who sees what, and the safe-feeling action (add a narrow Teacher access grant) does nothing if a wider role binding already exists. Two knobs that silently take the maximum is how data leaks happen while the admin believes it is locked.
findings.fix: Merge them into one "Access" surface per member showing the resolved list of classes that member can see, with the source of each grant labelled, and an explicit note that grants are additive. At minimum, cross-link the two pages and state "the widest grant wins" on both.

findings.title: A member can only be scoped to a whole top-level class, never to a single section or batch
findings.observed: The Scope dropdown listed exactly "Whole organization" and "Grade 10 (+ its sub-groups)", even though Section A and Section B exist under Grade 10. OrgRoles.jsx line 241 fetches listClasses({ parent: "none" }), so only top-level groups are ever offered, and the label explicitly commits to including all sub-groups.
findings.why_it_hurts: An institute's staffing unit is the batch, not the grade: one tutor takes Grade 11 Batch A evenings, another takes Batch B. The only isolation granularity on offer bundles every batch of that grade together, so the two tutors see each other's students and marks with no way to prevent it short of promoting each batch to a top-level class and losing the grouping.
findings.fix: Offer the full group tree in the Scope picker (indented sections under their class), and label the choice honestly: "Grade 10 · Section A" scopes to that section only, "Grade 10 (all sections)" for the parent.

findings.title: The audit log records nothing at all after a full session of org changes
findings.observed: During this audit I created a folder, added 3 students, created 2 sections, created an exam, attempted a staff invite (rejected on seat cap) and attempted to edit a system role (rejected). Afterwards the Audit log still reads "No audit entries — Audit events will appear here as members and admins take actions."
findings.why_it_hurts: The audit log is an admin-only page in the org rail, so an owner reasonably concludes it is the answer to "which tutor changed that answer key" or "who deleted Batch C". An empty log after real activity is worse than no page: it teaches the owner to trust a record that is not being kept.
findings.fix: Emit audit events for the writes that matter (member invited/removed/role changed, role binding assigned/revoked, class or exam created/deleted, answer key edited, results published), or hide the page behind a "coming soon" state until it does.

findings.title: Duplicate section and exam names are accepted silently, making the weekly-test list unnavigable
findings.observed: The exams table showed six rows all titled "Unit Test 3 Chemistry", all Whole class, all Attempt #1, all created Jul 27 2026 — distinguishable only by a Status chip (READY/DRAFT) and only two of the six have a Subject. The section filter dropdown listed "All sections, Whole class, Section A, Section B, Section B" — two identically named sections created without any duplicate warning. There is no date-time, no creator column, and no sort control on the exams table.
findings.why_it_hurts: An institute generates one or two exams per batch per week, so this table becomes hundreds of rows within a term. If "Weekly Test 12" appears three times because someone abandoned the wizard twice, the owner cannot tell which one has the real answer key or the real results, and a tutor will scan sheets into the wrong exam.
findings.fix: Warn on duplicate names within a class or section, show created time (not just date) plus the creator, add sorting on the exams table, and either auto-clean or clearly badge abandoned DRAFT exams with no questions.

findings.title: The Results page header shows a raw UUID instead of the exam title
findings.observed: The page heading is "Results" with the subtitle "Test #fc207ef7-e69d-42c3-af88-d38b07790e81". Every sibling page (Overview, Generate, Analytics, Review) uses the exam title "Midterm Physics" in exactly that slot, and the breadcrumb on this same page already shows "Midterm Physics".
findings.why_it_hurts: Results is the page an owner screenshots or shows to a parent. A 36-character UUID where the test name belongs looks unfinished, and with several same-named exams in a class it is also the one place the user most needs the human label.
findings.fix: Use the loaded test title for the subtitle, falling back to "Test" while loading, matching the other lifecycle pages.

findings.title: Row actions and the Retest control sit in a 28x28px button, under the 40px tap-target rule
findings.route: /classes/66084e86-.../exams, the "More test actions" kebab on each row
findings.observed: Measured the row controls: "Generate sheets" is 108x40 (fine) and the kebab labelled "More test actions" is 28x28. It hides Scan, Results, Review, Analytics and Retest — Retest being the only reachable way to create the next attempt of a weekly test, and the only thing that ever populates the Analytics Improvement tab. Desktop pages elsewhere carry 13 to 21 controls under 40px tall.
findings.why_it_hurts: The rule is tap targets ≥40px on every page. Beyond the miss, burying Retest behind an unlabeled 28px dot menu means the repeat-weekly-test workflow, which is the institute's whole cadence, is effectively undiscoverable — and the Improvement tab tells users to "create a retest" without saying where.
findings.fix: Raise the kebab to 40x40, and surface Retest as a labelled action on the exam Overview page's Lifecycle section ("Run this test again") so the weekly cadence is a first-class path.

findings.title: The organization dashboard is only a class grid, with no throughput signal for an owner
findings.observed: The org home is titled "Classes" and contains a search box plus class cards and a New class button. There are no totals (students, staff, tests this week), no pending review-queue count, no recently graded exams, no quota warning, and no activity feed. The only org-level numbers anywhere live on /usage, which shows seats, generations today and scans this cycle.
findings.why_it_hurts: An owner with 300 students and 4 staff opens the app to answer "what needs me today" — how many sheets are stuck in review, whose test has not been scanned, are we about to hit the scan quota mid-week. Instead they get a folder-style list and have to visit each class and each exam to find out.
findings.fix: Add a compact stat strip and an "Needs attention" list to the org dashboard: total students and staff, tests created and graded this week, sheets awaiting review across all classes (linked), and a quota warning when scans or generations pass 80%.

findings.title: The sole owner can remove themselves from their own organization with only a generic warning
findings.observed: With exactly one member (demo@doxaed.com, Owner, Active) the row still shows an enabled Remove button. It opens a correctly styled modal reading "Remove demo@doxaed.com from this organization? This cannot be undone." — with no mention that this is the last owner, or that the organization and its classes, students and results would be left with no administrator.
findings.why_it_hurts: One misclick on the wrong row and an institute locks itself out of its own data. The modal's wording gives no signal that this case is different from removing a tutor.
findings.fix: Disable Remove for the last remaining owner or admin with an explanatory tooltip, and if self-removal is allowed at all, require transferring ownership first.

area: First-run experience: logged-out marketing, register/verify/onboarding/create-org, and every empty state in a brand new org
worked: Empty states inside the org and class area are consistently built as title + one-line explanation + a primary CTA ("No classes yet / Create your first class to start adding exams, students and subjects / New class"), and the whole first-run path is genuinely responsive: zero horizontal overflow at both 320px and 390px across all 15 routes I swept, including the create-org plan picker and the generate page.

findings.title: The create-organization screen advertises plan limits that are invented and 5x looser than what the server enforces
findings.route: /organizations/new (the first screen inside the product for every new user), then /tests/:id/sheets
findings.observed: The Free plan card reads "₹0 · 1 seat · 50 students · 5 exams/mo". The real enforced Free limits (backend/billing/management/commands/seed_plans.py and backend/billing/limits.py) are 1 seat, 10 students per generation, 5 generations per DAY, 100 scans per month. I proved it end to end: signed up fresh, created org "Springfield High" on Free, added 11 students through the UI, clicked Generate sheets, and got POST /api/v1/omr/generate/ 403 {"detail":"Your plan allows up to 10 students per generation. Upgrade your plan to generate larger batches."}. Every tier is wrong the same way: the app says Pro = "500 students · 50 exams/mo" while the real Pro is unlimited students and 2,000 scans/month; Business says "2,000 students · 200 exams/mo" vs real unlimited students and 10,000 scans/month. The public /pricing page has the correct numbers, so the marketing site and the product's own signup screen contradict each other. The numbers are hardcoded in a PLANS const in NewOrganization.jsx, not fetched from GET /api/v1/billing/plans/ which already returns them.
findings.why_it_hurts: A school teacher with a class of 40 reads "50 students" on the signup screen, picks Free, spends 30 minutes typing 40 MCQs and adding a roster, then gets a 403 at the exact moment she is printing between periods. "5 exams/mo" and "5 generations per day" are not even the same unit, so she cannot plan around it either. The one number she needed to make a purchase decision was wrong in the direction that maximises wasted work.
findings.fix: Delete the hardcoded PLANS array in frontend/src/routes/NewOrganization.jsx and render the cards from GET /api/v1/billing/plans/ (it already returns seat_limit, students_per_generation_limit, generations_per_day_limit, monthly_scan_limit). Label them in the enforced units: "1 seat · 10 students per sheet run · 5 sheet runs/day · 100 scans/month". Add the same three-line quota summary to the Generate page.

findings.title: A finished 5-step onboarding wizard exists and works, but nothing in the app ever routes a new user to it
findings.observed: Register.jsx line 33 does navigate("/login") after signup; Login.jsx line 24 does navigate("/organizations") unconditionally. The only reference to "/onboarding" outside App.jsx is routes/Dashboard.jsx line 116, and Dashboard is not imported or mounted in App.jsx at all (/dashboard redirects to /classes). So the wizard at /onboarding (Welcome → Organisation → Invite → Class → Test) is dead code in practice. I drove it manually with a fresh account and it works fine end to end, producing an org, a class and a test. Instead, every real new user lands on a bare Organizations list.
findings.why_it_hurts: The product already contains the guided path that answers "what do I do next", and ships it switched off. A teacher who signs up gets an empty org list, then an empty class list, then an empty exam list, then an empty questions form, then a Generate page that says she has no roster - five consecutive dead ends that the wizard was written to walk her through.
findings.fix: In Login.jsx, after a successful login refresh the orgs list and, if the user has zero organizations and has not set the ONBOARDED_KEY flag, navigate to /onboarding instead of /organizations. Also add an "Set up my workspace" secondary link on the empty /organizations state.

findings.title: "Sign up with Google" is the largest, topmost control on both auth pages and it is dead, and its failure message leaks an internal env var name
findings.observed: Clicking it produces a toast: "Google sign-in isn't configured yet, add your Google client ID (VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID) to enable it." The button is rendered full-width above the email form on both pages, i.e. it is presented as the recommended path.
findings.why_it_hurts: The single most prominent action on the signup page does nothing. A user who defaults to social login (most people do) hits a wall on their first click, and the wall is a developer instruction addressed to someone else, which reads as "this product is unfinished" before they have seen a single feature.
findings.fix: Only render the Google button when import.meta.env.VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is set. If it must stay visible, disable it with the caption "Coming soon" and never surface the env var name to an end user.

findings.title: Abandoning the create-test wizard silently leaves a permanent phantom exam in the class, with no way to delete or tell them apart
findings.route: /classes/:id/tests/new → click "Next: Add questions" → navigate away; then /classes/:id/exams
findings.observed: The test row is POSTed when you leave step 1, not when you finish. During this audit I backed out of the wizard three times and ended with four rows in /classes/:id/exams, all titled "Unit Test 1", all dated the same day: one READY and three DRAFT. The exams table has no delete action (the only per-row control is "Generate sheets"), and the class Overview stat tile just says "EXAMS 4".
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who gets interrupted mid-setup (which is the normal case between periods) permanently pollutes the class. With 6 classes and weekly tests she accumulates dozens of identically named DRAFT ghosts and can no longer tell at a glance which "Unit Test 3" is the one she is about to print. There is no recovery inside the UI at all.
findings.fix: Create the Test only on "Finish & mark ready" (hold step-1 state client-side), or keep the draft but add a row delete action to /classes/:id/exams plus a server-side sweep of DRAFT tests with zero questions older than 24h. At minimum, disambiguate drafts in the table (created time, question count).

findings.title: The marketing headline feature "one question bank" does not exist in the product, and it is step 1 of the official getting-started guide
findings.route: /help step 1, /faq "How do I get started?", landing bento, /features → then anywhere in the app
findings.observed: Help.jsx step 1 says "Create a class and question bank. Start by creating a class and building its question bank, the pool of questions a test draws from." The landing bento says "One question bank. Write MCQs once; reuse across tests and sections." Grepping the whole repo, "question bank" appears ONLY in marketing files (Landing, Features, FAQ, Help, BuiltForPage). There is no question-bank model, route, API endpoint or UI: questions are typed inline per test in TestWizard step 2 and cannot be reused. Two neighbouring claims are also unreachable: Question.topic exists in backend/assessments/models.py line 214 but no exam UI ever renders a topic field (so the promised "per-topic mastery" and "per-topic accuracy" can never be populated), and a full Section model with per-section marking, qualify_pct and choose_k exists (lines 143-207) but the wizard has no paper-section builder, so "Competitive / sectional (NEET · UPSC style)" - a row in the /pricing comparison table - has no way in.
findings.why_it_hurts: A coaching-centre owner buys precisely on "write the bank once, reuse across weekly tests" and "per-topic accuracy". After paying she discovers she retypes every question for every test and the per-topic analytics she was shown can never have data. Worse for first run: the very first instruction in the product's own Help page tells her to build something that does not exist, so she spends her first ten minutes hunting for a missing menu item.
findings.fix: Either build it or stop selling it. Short term: rewrite Help step 1 to "Create a class, then add questions inside your first test", drop "One question bank" from the landing bento and Features, and remove the "Competitive / sectional papers" and per-topic rows from /pricing until there is UI. Medium term: add a topic input to the question editor (the column already exists) since it is the cheapest of the three to close.

findings.title: Review queue on a test that has never been scanned asserts "All caught up, all items resolved"
findings.route: /tests/:id/review on a brand new test with zero scans
findings.observed: The page renders the success empty state: heading "All caught up", body "All items resolved, no pending reviews.", and a "View results" button. Nothing has ever been uploaded for this test. It is indistinguishable from the state after a teacher has genuinely worked through a queue.
findings.why_it_hurts: The review queue is the single feature the marketing leans on for trust ("Never guessed, low-confidence reads go to review"). Telling a teacher "all items resolved" before a sheet exists trains her to skip the page. On a real test where a scan batch half-failed, she will read the same sentence and publish grades that were never reviewed. It is the one place in the app where a wrong empty state can produce a wrong grade.
findings.fix: Branch on whether any scan exists for the test. With zero scans show "Nothing to review yet, upload scanned sheets first" with a button to /tests/:id/scan. Reserve "All caught up" for the case where items existed and were resolved.

findings.title: Analytics on an ungraded test renders as a broken page, not an empty state, and offers three enabled export buttons
findings.route: /tests/:id/analytics on a test with 0 graded students
findings.observed: Stat tiles read STUDENTS 0, GRADED 0, AVERAGE n/a, MEDIAN n/a, NEEDS REVIEW 0; below them a full-size score-distribution chart draws its axes and gridlines with no bars; "Top performers" says "No toppers data available."; and "Export results" offers enabled Export CSV / Export Excel / Export PDF. There is no empty state, no explanation, and no link to Scan. A stray "0" also renders at the very bottom of the page.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the page a teacher opens first because it is the payoff the marketing sold. Seeing "n/a" over a blank chart with working export buttons reads as "the product is broken" rather than "you have not scanned yet", and she has no idea what to do next from here. The export buttons will hand her empty files she may attach to an email.
findings.fix: When graded == 0, replace the whole body with the standard empty state used elsewhere in the app: "No results to analyse yet / Upload scanned sheets to grade this test" plus a primary button to /tests/:id/scan. Disable or hide the export buttons at zero results, and remove the stray trailing "0".

findings.title: The Generate page's no-roster dead end uses a noun with no matching action, and the plan cap is never shown before you click
findings.route: /tests/:id/sheets on a class with no students, then with 11 students on Free
findings.observed: Two problems on the one page. (a) With no students it prints, in small grey body text under the "Roster" label, "This class has no rosters yet. Add one in the class, then come back to generate." There is no create-roster action in a class - you add Students and a roster materialises automatically named after the class - and the embedded link goes to the class Overview, not to /students. Meanwhile a separate /rosters page exists with its own "Create roster" CTA which is not what feeds this picker. Every other empty state in the app is a centred icon + heading + button; this one is an inline sentence that is easy to scroll past. (b) With 11 students on Free the page shows "11 of 11 selected" and a fully enabled Generate button, no cap indicator anywhere; the only feedback is an auto-dismissing toast after the 403, with no Upgrade link. The org Usage page has the right information ("Students per sheet generation is capped at 10 on this plan") but nothing on Generate links to it.
findings.why_it_hurts: (a) sends a first-run teacher to /rosters where she creates a standalone roster that will never appear in this picker. (b) means the failure lands at print time, as a message that vanishes in four seconds, with no path to fixing it - she has to guess that the answer is deselecting students or upgrading.
findings.fix: (a) Use the app's standard empty-state component: "No students in this class yet" with a primary button linking directly to /classes/:id/students, and use the word students, not rosters. (b) Show the cap inline next to the selection counter ("11 of 11 selected · Free plan allows 10 per run"), turn the counter red past the cap, disable Generate, and put an Upgrade link next to it.

findings.title: /folders is completely unreachable in the shipped UI although it is sold on the pricing page
findings.observed: nav-config.js defines exactly two rail sections, Classes and Settings. Folders has no nav entry, and unlike Rosters and Scan it also has no Cmd-K action (CommandMenu.jsx has "action new roster" → /rosters and "action scan" → /scan, but nothing for folders). Grepping all JSX, the only mention of folders outside its own route files is an API import in NewClass.jsx. Yet "Folders & sharing" is a row in the /pricing comparison table and a footer capability link, and the page itself is fully built with a proper empty state ("No folders yet / Create a folder to organise your classes, and share whole folders with colleagues / New folder"). Rosters and Scan are only marginally better: reachable via Cmd-K actions, which do not exist on a phone.
findings.why_it_hurts: A coaching-institute owner who bought partly on "share whole folders with colleagues" cannot find the feature at all, and support has no answer other than "type the URL". More broadly, Scan is the daily job of this product and it has no navigation entry on mobile, which is the device the marketing insists you use.
findings.fix: Add Folders, Rosters and Scan as rail sections (or as a group under the Classes section) in frontend/src/components/shell/nav-config.js, and add Folders to the Cmd-K Actions group. Scan in particular should also appear in the mobile bottom navigation.

findings.title: Every logged-out page paints large gradients, violating the no-gradients rule on the whole first-run surface
findings.observed: Each of these pages renders a full-width 420-560px radial-gradient indigo glow behind the hero, e.g. on the landing: radial-gradient(60% 50% at 50% 0%, oklch(0.482074 0.287269 273.42 / 0.14), rgba(0,0,0,0) 72%), plus a second radial-gradient band lower down, plus animated linear-gradient overlays on the .landing-scanline elements. Measured live via getComputedStyle across every public route. In-app pages measured clean (0 gradients), so the violation is confined to the marketing and auth surface - which is exactly the surface a first-run user sees.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is a stated non-negotiable owner rule (flat solid colours only, no gradients anywhere), broken on 15 pages including the two auth screens. It is also the only visual inconsistency between the marketing site and the app, so the product feels like a different piece of software the moment you log in.
findings.fix: Replace the hero glow divs with a flat solid tinted band (a single background-color at the same perceived lightness) and drop the .landing-scanline linear-gradient animation in favour of a solid translucent bar, in the shared PublicLayout/AuthLayout hero and in index.css.

findings.title: Registration ends on an empty login form, and the email verification it tells you to do is never enforced, never nudged, and cannot be resent
findings.observed: After a successful signup the app navigates to /login with the toast "Account created, check your email to verify" and an empty email/password form - you retype both credentials you just chose. I then signed in immediately without verifying and got full access with no banner, no badge and no prompt anywhere in the app. There is no resend affordance: grepping "resend" returns zero hits in frontend/src and zero in backend/accounts. /verify-email with no token at all shows the same "Link invalid - This verification link is invalid or has expired" as a genuinely bad token, with only a "Back to sign in" link.
findings.why_it_hurts: The user is told to do something that turns out to be optional, is given no way to redo it when the mail does not arrive, and pays a retyping tax on the way in. A teacher whose verification mail lands in spam has no recovery path except signing up again with a different address.
findings.fix: Auto-login after registration (the API already returns tokens on login; do the same on register) or at minimum prefill the email on /login. Add a POST /auth/resend-verification endpoint with a "Resend verification email" button on /verify-email and in an in-app banner for unverified accounts. Distinguish the no-token case ("Open the link from your verification email") from the invalid-token case.

findings.title: Results and Review pages label themselves with the raw test UUID instead of the test name
findings.observed: Both pages render description={`Test #${testId}`}, producing the subtitle "Test #22e60ebe-2cee-4d92-b64d-d5e2f62c5111". Every sibling tab in the same lifecycle (Overview, Questions, Generate, Analytics) correctly shows "Unit Test 1".
findings.why_it_hurts: Results is the page a teacher screenshots or shows to a colleague, and it is the only one that does not say which test it is. A 36-character hex string where the exam name should be reads as a debug build, right at the moment the teacher is deciding whether to trust the scores.
findings.fix: Fetch the test (both pages already have the id) and pass description={test.title} like ExamOverview and Analytics do. Results.jsx line 544, ReviewQueue.jsx line 152.

findings.title: Every browser tab in the product is titled "frontend"
findings.observed: frontend/index.html line 7 is <title>frontend</title> and nothing in src ever sets document.title (no react-helmet, no useDocumentTitle, no document.title assignment). Confirmed live across 17 public routes and every in-app route I visited.
findings.why_it_hurts: The workflow this product sells is inherently multi-tab: exam open, scan open, results open, plus the printed PDF. All four tabs read "frontend", so the teacher tab-hunts by favicon alone. It also means every marketing page shares one meaningless title in search results and in bookmarks.
findings.fix: Set a real default in index.html ("DoxaEd OMR") and add a small title hook that sets document.title per route, e.g. "Unit Test 1 · Results · DoxaEd OMR".

findings.title: The two organisation-creation paths produce different vocabularies for the same product
findings.observed: /organizations/new asks for a Type (School → "Classes › Sections", Coaching → "Batches › Sections", etc.) and the resulting workspace says "Classes / No classes yet / New class". The onboarding wizard never asks for a type, so its org falls back to generic labels: creating "Sunrise Coaching" through /onboarding produced "Groups in Sunrise Coaching / No groups yet / Create your first group / New group". "Group" appears nowhere in the marketing, which talks exclusively about classes, batches and rosters.
findings.why_it_hurts: Two users at the same coaching centre, onboarded through different doors, end up using different words for the same object, and neither matches the Help page they were pointed at. The wizard - the path meant to be the friendliest - produces the least recognisable vocabulary.
findings.fix: Add the same Type picker to onboarding step 2, or default the wizard's org type from a light question ("What are you grading for?") so the labels match /organizations/new and the marketing copy.

findings.title: The question editor defaults to 2 options when the data model defaults to 4, and the Add-student modal marks the optional field rather than the required one
findings.observed: Every new question card renders options A and B only, so each question needs two "+ Add option" clicks to reach the normal four-choice MCQ - 80 extra clicks on a 40-question paper. Test.default_options in backend/assessments/models.py line 83 is already 4, and the marketing lists "4 or 5 options" as a supported mode. Separately, the Add-student modal labels the first field "Full name (optional)" and the second plain "Roll number"; roll number is the required one - filling only the name and submitting produces the toast "Roll number is required".
findings.why_it_hurts: The option default is pure repetitive tax on the longest, most tedious task in the product, at the moment a first-run user is deciding whether this is faster than marking by hand. The modal labelling actively misleads: the only field marked is the one you can skip, so the first student a teacher ever adds fails to save.
findings.fix: Seed new question cards with the test's default_options (4) and keep the remove buttons for anyone who wants fewer. In the student modal, mark "Roll number" as required (asterisk or "required" hint) and validate inline on blur rather than only via a toast after submit.

area: Mobile / phone-first experience (390x844 and 320x568, touch emulation, real Chromium)
worked: Sign-in and the exam Overview hub are genuinely good on a phone: full-width fields, a clear READY badge, and a 70px-tall tappable "Lifecycle" list with an actionable "Some questions have no correct answer set. Fix the answer key" banner.

findings.title: The review queue is unreachable on a phone: no link to it exists anywhere below the lg breakpoint
findings.route: /tests/fc207ef7.../review (reachable only by typing the URL). Checked: bottom tab bar, hamburger drawer on 3 different pages, exam Overview Lifecycle list, command menu search for "review"
findings.observed: The route renders fine, but nothing in the mobile UI points at it. The bottom tab bar has exactly three items (Classes, Organizations, Account). The hamburger drawer returns the same two entries on every page I opened it, including while standing on the exam's own Scan page: "Doxaed Demo School | Admin | Classes | Settings". The exam Overview Lifecycle list has five cards (Edit questions, Generate & print, Scan sheets, Results, Analytics) and no Review. Typing "review" into the command menu returns "No results found." A six-stage rail that does include Review already exists in components/ui/test-progress-rail.jsx, but it is only fed into the secondary nav panel, which is styled "hidden ... lg:flex", and a grep shows no route in the app links to /tests/:id/review at all.
findings.why_it_hurts: The product's whole trust claim is that low-confidence bubble reads go to a review queue and are never guessed. Scanning happens on the phone, so the phone is exactly where a teacher discovers flagged sheets, and it is the one place they cannot open the queue to resolve them. A teacher standing next to the photocopier either publishes scores that contain unresolved reads or walks back to a desktop.
findings.fix: Render the existing TestProgressRail (it is already "-mx-4 overflow-x-auto" and mobile-ready) directly under PageHeader on every /tests/:testId/* page below lg, add a sixth "Review" card to the ExamOverview Lifecycle list with a count badge of pending items, and register a "Review queue" command in CommandMenu.

findings.title: The scan step fails and the phone is told nothing but a 3-second "Upload failed" toast
findings.observed: POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/omr/scan/ returns 500 with Django's debug HTML; the exception is ImportError('Unable to find zbar shared library'), so the QR decode path is dead and no sheet can be graded (results_studentresult is empty for every test in the DB). What the phone shows is a bottom toast reading exactly "Upload failed" (y=736, h=93 in an 844px viewport, so it sits on top of the bottom nav and on top of the button just pressed), which auto-dismisses in about five seconds. After that the page looks identical to before: the file is still listed, the button is still enabled, there is no inline error, no reason, no retry, no "contact support".
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the step the product exists for and the step that happens on a phone in a corridor between periods. A two-word toast that disappears while the teacher is still holding the next sheet gives them nothing to act on, so they re-tap, re-tap again, and conclude the app is broken. Even once zbar is installed, any real-world failure (bad photo, no network, plan limit) will surface the same way.
findings.fix: Install the zbar shared library in the backend image and return a JSON error body instead of Django HTML. On the client, replace the toast-only path with a persistent inline error block above the upload button that names the cause and offers "Try again", keep the selected files, and never let a 500 HTML body be swallowed into a generic string.

findings.title: Every checkbox, radio and switch is visually deformed and under-sized on phones by a blanket min-height rule
findings.route: /tests/fc207ef7.../sheets (student checkboxes, Shuffle switches) and /tests/fc207ef7.../questions (the "select one correct answer" radios)
findings.observed: index.css applies `min-height: 40px` to every `button` under a 768px media query. shadcn's Checkbox, RadioGroupItem and Switch are all rendered as buttons, so they get stretched vertically only. Measured the same page at two widths: Switch 32x18 at 1440px becomes 32x40 at 390px; Checkbox 16x16 becomes 16x40; RadioGroupItem 16x16 becomes 16x40. On screen the student checkboxes are tall blue capsules and the Shuffle toggles are round blobs whose on/off state is no longer legible as a switch. They also still fail the 40px rule on the other axis (16px and 32px wide).
findings.why_it_hurts: The answer-key radio is the single most consequential control in the product: pick the wrong one and every sheet is graded against a wrong key. On a phone it is a 16px-wide sliver that does not read as a radio button. The Generate page's per-student checkboxes are the same sliver, so deselecting one student out of forty is a game of precision tapping.
findings.fix: Exclude the toggle primitives from the blanket rule (`button:not([data-slot=checkbox]):not([data-slot=radio-group-item]):not([data-slot=switch])`) and instead give each primitive a real touch target: a 40x40 transparent hit area around the visual control (padding or a ::before overlay), keeping the visual box square/pill at its designed size.

findings.title: List cards are not tappable; the only way into an exam is a 16px-tall text link
findings.observed: Each exam renders as a card, but tapping anywhere in the card body does nothing (URL unchanged). The only target is the title text itself, measured at 134x16 px for "Unit Test 3 Chemistry" and 104x16 for "Midterm Physics" at a 390px viewport. DataTable only gives its mobile card `role="button"` when an `onRowClick` prop is passed, and a grep shows no route in the app passes it. The only hint that a card is interactive is `hover:bg-muted/50`, which does nothing on touch.
findings.why_it_hurts: Opening an exam is the most repeated action in the app and on a phone it is a 16px-high target with no visual affordance, well under the thumb's accuracy. A teacher with six exams named similarly will mis-tap repeatedly and land back on the same list.
findings.fix: Pass `onRowClick` from the exam, roster and folder lists so the whole card becomes the target, give the card a min-height of 56px, promote the first column to a card heading, and add a right-hand chevron so tappability is visible without hover.

findings.title: Mobile list cards are a mechanical transposition of the desktop table, so the exam name is a right-aligned value under a "Title" label
findings.observed: DataTable's sub-md renderer turns every column into a "label ......... value" row, right-aligned, with no primary field. An exam card therefore reads: Title / Unit Test 3 Chemistry, Subject / n/a, Section / Whole class, Status / READY, Attempt / #1, Created / Jul 27 2026. Six exams make the page 3,378px tall. `hideOnMobile` is supported by the component but is not used by a single route, so nothing is ever dropped. On /rosters two of three cards read "Name / Students" because the label and the value are indistinguishable.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher scanning for "the physics midterm" has to read the right-hand edge of six near-identical blocks and scroll through half a metre of screen. The word that matters is the least prominent thing on the card, and low-value columns (Attempt, Created) consume the same visual weight as the exam name.
findings.fix: Give DataTable a `primaryColumn` that renders as a left-aligned card heading with no label, mark Attempt/Created/Subject `hideOnMobile`, and put status as a badge on the heading row. Cap the mobile card at heading + two supporting facts + status.

findings.title: Questions editor is a 3,500px wall on a phone and its "Save all" bar never actually sticks
findings.observed: All ten questions render fully expanded; the document is 3,462px tall at 390px wide, roughly 245px per question. The footer is `sticky bottom-0 z-20` but the scrolling container is the window and the bar's containing block ends where the bar sits, so it never pins: after scrolling to 400px I measured the bar at document y=2973 with the viewport at 844px, and the screenshot at that scroll position shows no save bar at all. Its z-index (20) is also below the fixed bottom nav (z-40), so even when it does appear it is competing with the tab bar for the same 57px strip. Editing question 8 means scrolling roughly 1,900px down and, if you want "Save all", another 1,500px.
findings.why_it_hurts: Fixing one wrong answer key entry between periods becomes a long scroll hunt with no way to jump to a question and no persistent save. Each card also shows a purple "Saved" button next to green "Saved" text, so it is unclear whether anything still needs saving.
findings.fix: Collapse questions to one-line rows on mobile (number, first words of the text, the key letter) that expand on tap, add a question jump control, and make the save bar genuinely fixed to the viewport bottom sitting above the tab bar (or fold the tab bar away on this page).

findings.title: The scan screen leads with a desktop drag-and-drop zone; the camera, the actual phone action, is a small secondary button
findings.observed: The dominant element is a large dashed box labelled "Drop sheet images or PDFs here" with "or click to browse" beneath it. The camera is a `size="sm"` outline button labelled "Camera (mobile)" sitting under it at roughly a third of the width. Selected files appear as plain file-name text ("fake-sheet.png"), never as thumbnails, and there is no capture guidance anywhere on the page (framing, lighting, keep the QR corner visible) and no preview or quality check before uploading. The page description also says "Use the lifecycle panel to move between stages" while no lifecycle panel exists at this width.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher photographing forty sheets is being asked to drag and drop on a device with no drag and drop, then hand a stack of blind uploads to a grader that will reject bad photos one at a time. Camera captures are named IMG_0042.jpg, so the file-name list tells them nothing about which sheets are in the batch.
