findings.fix: On touch viewports promote the camera to the full-width primary action, demote the dropzone to a text link, show captured photos as a thumbnail grid with per-item remove, add two lines of capture guidance beside it, and replace the lifecycle sentence with copy that matches what is on screen.

findings.title: There is no Scan entry in the mobile navigation even though scanning is the phone job
findings.route: Bottom tab bar on every page
findings.observed: BOTTOM_TABS is Classes, Organizations, Account. Getting to a scan from a cold start is Classes, tap class, tap Exams, tap exam, tap "Scan sheets" (five taps). The only shortcut is the command menu's "Scan sheets" action, reached through a magnifier icon in the header that a teacher is unlikely to try. "Organizations" occupies a permanent third of the tab bar for something a single-school teacher opens roughly never.
findings.why_it_hurts: For the coaching institute running weekly tests, scanning is the daily repeated action and it is buried five taps deep behind an org switcher.
findings.fix: Make the tab bar Classes / Scan / Account and move Organizations into the drawer or the account menu; have the Scan tab open the last active exam's scan page, falling back to the test picker.

findings.title: Stat cards stack one per row below 640px, so the first phone screen of every class and exam is four numbers
findings.observed: Both overviews use `grid grid-cols-1 gap-6 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-4`, and Tailwind's sm breakpoint is 640px, so every phone gets one column. On the class page that is roughly 510px of Exams/Students/Sections/Subjects before the first button; on the exam page the four cards plus the answer-key warning push the first Lifecycle action ("Edit questions") to y=640 in an 844px viewport. Analytics, by contrast, uses a 2-up grid and reads fine.
findings.why_it_hurts: Every visit to a class or an exam starts with a scroll past four numbers nobody opened the page for. On a 320x568 phone the actions are entirely below the fold.
findings.fix: Start the KPI grid at `grid-cols-2` with `gap-3`, and on the exam page move the Lifecycle list above the stats so the first screen is actions.

findings.title: Desktop type density is shipped unchanged to phones: status and identity text renders at 11px, tab labels at 10px
findings.route: Every page; measured computed font sizes at 390px
findings.observed: The theme sets --text-xs to 0.6875rem (11px) and --text-sm to 0.8125rem (13px). At 11px on a phone: student roll numbers ("001"), "10 of 10 selected", the green "Saved" confirmation on each question, the READY/DRAFT status badges, "Whole class", "14 students", "View all", and the "Generate" buttons in Recent exams. The bottom tab labels are hard-coded `text-[10px]` and the chart axis labels render at 10px.
findings.why_it_hurts: Roll number and READY/DRAFT are the two facts a teacher must not misread: the roll number is what the printed sheet is keyed on, and the status is what tells them the exam is safe to print. Reading them at 11px on a phone held at arm's length in a bright classroom is where mistakes come from.
findings.fix: Raise the floor on touch viewports: a media query that lifts --text-xs to 12px and --text-sm to 14px below 768px, and take the tab labels to 11-12px. Keep the dense scale for desktop where it belongs.

findings.title: Toasts are the only feedback channel and they land on top of the bottom nav and the button just pressed
findings.observed: The toast renders at y=736, height 93, in an 844px viewport, i.e. covering the whole 787-844 fixed tab bar and the "Generate sheets" button underneath it. The message was "Daily generation limit reached for your organisation's plan. Upgrade your plan for more daily generations." with no Upgrade link, no inline echo on the page, and it disappears on a timer. Nothing on the page changes to record that generation failed.
findings.why_it_hurts: For the few seconds it is up, the teacher cannot use the navigation at all. Once it is gone there is no trace: the page looks the same as a successful run, so a teacher may walk to the printer believing sheets exist. Errors that block the job need to persist, and blocking errors that have a remedy (upgrade) need the remedy attached.
findings.fix: Position toasts above the tab bar (bottom offset of nav height + safe-area) and never over the primary action. For blocking errors, render a persistent inline banner in the card that failed, with the remedy as a button ("View plans").

findings.title: The Generate page's student picker is a 224px keyhole over the roster, with no select-all or search
findings.observed: The picker is an inner scroll box measured at 224px tall over a 514px list, so about four and a half of ten students are visible and the fifth row is sliced in half by the box edge. It is a nested scroller inside a page that also scrolls, which on touch means a drag started on a student row scrolls the inner list and a drag started 10px away scrolls the page. The only bulk control is "Clear all" (11px text); there is no select-all-in-section, no search, and no count of what will print beyond an 11px "10 of 10 selected".
findings.why_it_hurts: With 40 students the teacher scrolls a 2,000px list through a 224px window on a device where the scroll gesture is ambiguous, just to reprint sheets for the three who were absent. That is exactly the everyday case.
findings.fix: Let the list grow inline on mobile instead of nesting a scroller, add a search field and a select-all/none control with a section filter, and put the "N of M selected" count next to the Generate button at body size.

findings.title: Analytics tables will need sideways scrolling with no frozen first column, and one tab renders nothing at all
findings.observed: The Improvement tab renders literally nothing below the tab strip: no chart, no table, no empty state (the other tabs at least say "No results available for this test"). The per-item psychometrics table sets fixed widths w-12 + w-28 + w-28 + w-32 plus a flexible Flags column, i.e. about 400px of columns inside a 358px content width at 390px, in a plain `overflow-x-auto` wrapper with no sticky Q# column; toppers is five columns and hardest-questions carries a free-text Question column alongside w-28 and w-20 columns. The tab strip itself needs 375px in a 288px viewport at 320px, so "Improvement" is completely offscreen with no scroll affordance. I could not populate real results because the scan endpoint is down, so the table widths are measured from the layout rather than from rendered rows.
findings.why_it_hurts: A blank tab reads as a broken app. And once results exist, reading discrimination or point-biserial means swiping right, at which point the question number scrolls out of view, so the numbers cannot be attributed to a question without swiping back.
findings.fix: Give the Improvement tab a real empty state. Below md, render each analytics table as a card per question (Q number as the heading, metrics as labelled rows) instead of a horizontally scrolling table, or at minimum freeze the Q# column and add a visible scroll affordance. Add fading edge hints to the tab strip.

findings.title: Results and Review pages identify the exam by raw UUID, which wraps to two lines on a phone
findings.observed: The subtitle reads "Test #fc207ef7-e69d-42c3-af88-d38b07790e81" and wraps across two lines at 390px, pushing the content down, while the sibling pages (Analytics, Generate) correctly show "Midterm Physics". The Generate page proves the title is already available at this level.
findings.why_it_hurts: On a phone the header is the only context there is, and a teacher juggling several tests sees a hex string instead of the exam they opened. It also makes screenshots useless when a teacher forwards results to a colleague.
findings.fix: Fetch the test and use its title as the PageHeader description on Results and ReviewQueue, matching Analytics.

findings.title: At 320px page titles truncate to meaninglessness because the header action shares the row
findings.observed: PageHeader's h1 carries `truncate`; at 320px "Generate OMR sheets" needs 207px but gets 142px and renders as "Generate O…" while the "Back to class" button takes the rest of the row. On the exam Overview the lifecycle subtitles clip too ("Add or change questions & answer key" needs 203px in 178px).
findings.why_it_hurts: On the smallest phones still in classroom use, the title of the page tells the teacher nothing, and the header action getting priority over the title is backwards.
findings.fix: Below sm, stack PageHeader as title on its own row with the action full width beneath it, and allow the h1 to wrap to two lines instead of truncating.

findings.title: Class Students on a phone is read-only: no way to open, edit or delete a student
findings.observed: Tapping "Asha Rao" does nothing (URL unchanged) and the page's complete set of controls is: Add student, the All sections filter, and the search box. There is no kebab, no edit, no delete, and nothing is hidden behind hover (I checked for group-hover reveals and found none anywhere in the codebase), so this is a genuine absence rather than a touch problem.
findings.why_it_hurts: The roll number is the key the OMR sheet is printed and matched against. A teacher who typos one while adding students on a phone has no path to correct it from the only student screen the phone offers.
findings.fix: Make the row open a student detail sheet, and add rename / change-roll / move-section / remove actions in a row kebab that meets the 40px target.

findings.title: New class modal at 320x568 hides its primary button below the fold with no scroll cue
findings.observed: The dialog is 511px tall over 641px of content (inner scroll present) and the "Create class" button measures at y=613 with the viewport at 568, so it is below the fold. The dialog has no sticky footer and no shadow or fade to indicate more content, and the visible bottom edge of the card looks like the end of the form. At 390x844 the same modal fits, so this only bites the smallest phones (and any phone once the soft keyboard is up).
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher creating their first class on a small phone sees a form that appears complete with no way to submit it, and abandoning at first-run onboarding is the worst place to lose someone.
findings.fix: Pin the dialog footer with the primary action so it is always visible, and add a scroll shadow on the scrollable body.

findings.title: The list count chip is hidden behind the first card, leaving a stray empty outline
findings.route: /rosters at 390px (same pattern on /organizations and the org audit page)
findings.observed: The "3 rosters" chip sits in a `-mb-4` wrapper at y=164 with the card list starting at y=168, so the card covers the chip and only the top few pixels of its border show as an empty rounded box poking out of the card's top-left corner. The count text is unreadable. It reproduces at 1440px too.
findings.why_it_hurts: It reads as a rendering bug on the first screen of a list page, which is a small but direct hit to how finished the product feels, and the count itself is lost.
findings.fix: Drop the negative margin and place the count chip inside the PageHeader row (or above the list with normal spacing).

findings.title: The sheet corrector's answer buttons are 32px, under the touch minimum, on the most precision-critical action
findings.route: components/SheetCorrectorPanel.jsx (could not be driven: no graded sheets exist because the scan endpoint is down)
findings.observed: The per-question option buttons in the corrector table are `min-h-[32px] min-w-[32px]` with `text-xs` (11px) labels, inside a dialog capped at 95dvh whose image pane takes max-h-[50dvh] on mobile and whose answer column then gets its own inner scroll. The standalone ReviewQueue page does this correctly at min-h/min-w 40px, so the two review surfaces disagree.
findings.why_it_hurts: Correcting a misread bubble is the action where a wrong tap silently changes a student's score. Doing it on 32px squares, in an 11px grid, in a panel with three nested scroll regions, is where a teacher stops trusting the grade.
findings.fix: Raise the corrector's option buttons to 40x40 with 13px labels to match ReviewQueue, and on mobile split the corrector into two full-height steps (look at the photo, then answer) rather than stacking a 50dvh image over a scrolling answer column.

area: OMR sheet generation (Generate & print page, /tests/:testId/sheets) and the PDFs it produces
worked: Per student selection is genuinely good: the roster loads with everyone pre-checked, Select all / Clear all works, the button relabels itself to "Generate 7 sheets", and generation of 7 shuffled sheets plus per student question papers completed in 882 ms with a correct, correctly shuffled question paper per student.

findings.title: Roster pre-bubbled mode prints the WRONG roll number on every sheet (all students get "00")
findings.route: /tests/518bfa09-7aeb-485d-81e0-d3be1dfef189/sheets → Generate sheets, on a test created with mode=roster_prebubbled, roster of 10 students with roll numbers 001..010
findings.observed: Every generated sheet has an identical pre-filled roll grid reading "00". Student 4 (roll 004) and Student 7 (roll 007) both print two filled bubbles in the 0-row of a 2-column grid. Root cause is in GenerateView: roll_digits = max(2, len(str(max_roll_int))) derives the grid width from the integer value of the largest roll (10 → 2 columns), while roll_value = student_roll.zfill(roll_digits) never truncates, so "004" (3 chars) is handed to a 2-column grid. render_sheet_pdf then does `if col_idx >= cols: break`, silently dropping the third digit and printing only "0","0". Verified in the DB: template_descriptor->roll_grid->cols = 2 while roll_value = '004','007' etc. for all 7 sheets.
findings.why_it_hurts: Roster pre-bubbled exists for exactly one reason: the sheet carries the student's identity so scanning auto-identifies them without the student writing anything. Here every sheet in the batch carries the same wrong identity. Leading-zero roll numbers (001, 002, ...) are the normal case in Indian schools and coaching institutes, and the seeded demo roster uses them too, so this fires on the default data. A teacher prints 40 sheets, hands them out, and only discovers at grading time that the printed roll does not match the student, or that a human checking the sheet against the register sees garbage.
findings.fix: Compute roll_digits from the maximum *string* length of the roster's roll numbers, not from the integer value: roll_digits = max(2, max(len(s.roll_number or '') for s in students)). Additionally make the truncation loud instead of silent: if len(roll_value) > cols, raise a 400 with "Roll number 004 does not fit the 2 column roll grid" rather than printing a wrong sheet. Add a regression test that a roster of 001..010 produces a 3 column grid and that sheet.roll_value == the digits actually drawn.

findings.title: Generation quota is invisible until you hit it, and there is no way to re-open a batch you already generated
findings.observed: Clicking Generate produced a toast: "Daily generation limit reached for your organisation's plan. Upgrade your plan for more daily generations." Nothing anywhere on the page hinted a quota existed. The free plan is 5 generations/day and 10 students per generation (billing/limits.py), but the org creation screen advertises the free plan only as "1 seat · 50 students · 5 exams/mo" and never mentions either generation cap. Worse: reloading the Generate page shows no trace of the batch you generated two minutes ago (verified: after a successful generation, a fresh visit to the same URL shows no success panel and no download link). The batch URL lives only in React state. listSheets() exists in /frontend/src/api/omr.js and GET /omr/sheets/?test= exists on the server, but nothing in the frontend ever calls them.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher printing between periods clicks Generate, the tab reloads or they navigate to check the roster, and the PDF is gone. The only way to get it back is to generate again, which burns another of the 5 daily generations and, if the answer key changed in between, silently rewrites the sheets. A 40-student class cannot be printed at all on the free plan (10 students per generation, so 4 generations, leaving 1 for the rest of the day across all 6 classes). The user has no way to plan around a limit they cannot see.
findings.fix: (1) Show remaining quota inline above the Generate button: "3 of 5 generations left today · up to 10 students per generation · resets 00:00", sourced from a small /billing/usage endpoint, and disable the button with that reason when exhausted. (2) Make the error toast a modal with the actual numbers and a direct link to Billing. (3) Add a "Previously generated" list on this page driven by listSheets(test), showing each student, sheet code, generated-at, and a per-sheet print link, so reprinting never costs a generation.

findings.title: The print packet comes out in random order and contains students you deliberately deselected
findings.route: /tests/518bfa09-7aeb-485d-81e0-d3be1dfef189/sheets → deselect students 8, 9, 10 → Generate 7 sheets → "Download print packet (questions + sheets)"
findings.observed: The 21-page packet is ordered Student 4, 7, 6, 1, 2, 5, 3 — completely scrambled. The "Download sheets PDF" batch from the same click is in roll order 001, 002, 003... So the two PDFs the page hands you are in different orders. Cause: OmrTestQuestionPapersBatchView does `OmrSheet.objects.filter(test=test).order_by("id")` on a UUID primary key. That same query also ignores the student subset entirely: it returns every sheet ever generated for the test, so on a second generation for a different subset the packet includes students you unchecked and stale sheets from an earlier run. Each student's packet is 3 pages (2 paper + 1 sheet), an odd number, with no blank padding, so duplex printing puts one student's answer sheet on the back of the next student's question paper.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher's job after clicking download is to walk into a room and hand each student their own sheet. Scrambled order means manually re-sorting 40 packets by name. Including deselected students means printing sheets for absentees you explicitly excluded. Odd page counts mean duplex (the school default) shuffles students across sheet boundaries and the packet has to be reprinted single-sided, doubling paper.
findings.fix: Order the packet by the roster's roll_number (join through student and order_by('student__roll_number','student__id')) so it matches the sheets PDF. Accept the student_ids subset (or a generation batch id) as a query param and filter to it, defaulting to the last generation. Pad each student's packet to an even page count with a blank page so duplex printing keeps one student per physical sheet.

findings.title: Nothing tells the teacher how to print, and wrong printer settings silently break OMR reading
findings.observed: The success panel offers "Open & print", "Download sheets PDF" and "Download print packet" with zero print guidance. The page never mentions A4, 100% scale, "do not fit to page", margins, single-sided, or that a laser printer is preferred over an inkjet. The sheet geometry is a fixed A4 100 DPI grid with four corner fiducials at exactly 52px from the edge, and the scan aligner keys off those fiducials.
findings.why_it_hurts: Chrome's PDF print dialog defaults to "Fit to printable area", which shrinks the page by ~4% and shifts every fiducial and bubble. The teacher prints 40 sheets, students fill them, and the scan step fails to align or drops confidence on every read, with no clue why. This is the single cheapest way for a user to lose trust in the score, and it is entirely preventable with one line of copy.
findings.fix: Put a short, non-dismissable note in the success panel: "Print on A4 at 100% scale. Turn off Fit to page or Scale to fit, and print single sided." Also stamp the same line in small type in the bottom margin of page 1 of every generated sheet so the instruction survives being emailed to an office assistant.

findings.title: "Use organisation logo and heading" is a no-op once a test heading has ever been saved
findings.route: /tests/518bfa09-7aeb-485d-81e0-d3be1dfef189/sheets → toggle org branding off → type "MY CUSTOM SCHOOL" → Save branding → toggle org branding back ON → Save branding → Generate sheets
findings.observed: Verified live: with the toggle ON and saved, the generated PDF still prints "MY CUSTOM SCHOOL" as the sheet heading. In GenerateView the resolution is `if test_heading: use it; elif org_fresh: use org heading` — brand_inherit_org only gates whether the org is *fetched*, it never stops the test-level heading or logo from winning. The frontend compounds it: handleSaveBranding for inherit=true deliberately PATCHes only {brand_inherit_org: true} and leaves sheet_heading/logo intact, and the heading input is hidden while the toggle is on, so the teacher cannot see or clear the value that is actually being printed.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher sees a toggle that says the org logo will be used, flips it, saves, sees a "Branding saved" success toast, prints 40 sheets, and the wrong school name is on every one. There is no way to undo it from this page short of toggling off, clearing the field by hand, and saving again, which is not discoverable because the field is hidden in the state you are in.
findings.fix: Make brand_inherit_org authoritative on the server: when it is true, ignore test.sheet_heading / test.logo entirely and resolve from the org. Keep the stored test values so flipping back restores them. In the UI, when the toggle is ON, show a read-only preview line: "Will print: <org heading> with <org logo>" (or "Your organisation has no heading or logo set. Add one in Settings."), so the teacher can see the actual outcome.

findings.title: Shuffle is ON by default with no explanation, and the primary print button prints only the answer sheets
findings.route: /tests/:testId/sheets → "Shuffle questions" and "Shuffle options" toggles → Generate sheets → success panel
findings.observed: Both shuffle switches default to ON. There is no helper text explaining what shuffling does, and nothing warns that shuffling makes each student's question order different, so a single shared printed question paper no longer matches any sheet. The consequence only appears after generation, as a third, outline-styled button labelled "Download print packet (questions + sheets)", while the solid primary button is "Open & print", which opens the answer sheets alone.
findings.why_it_hurts: The overwhelmingly likely first-run path is: leave the defaults, click Generate, click the big primary "Open & print", print 40 answer sheets, and hand them out alongside the question paper the teacher already had printed. Every student is now answering question 1 in an order that does not match their sheet, and the auto-grading will mark almost everything wrong. The teacher has no way to know before clicking, because nothing on the page connects the shuffle toggles to the need for per-student papers.
findings.fix: Add helper text under the toggles that changes live: with shuffle on, "Each student gets a different question order, so each student needs their own printed question paper. Use Download print packet." With shuffle off, "All students get the same order, so one shared question paper works." When shuffle is on, make "Download print packet" the solid primary action and demote "Open & print" / "Download sheets PDF" to outline.

findings.title: No preview: a teacher cannot see a single sheet before committing a generation
findings.observed: The page has branding controls, a roster picker, a student list and two shuffle toggles, and then a Generate button. There is no sample sheet, no thumbnail, no "preview one sheet" action. The teacher cannot see the heading placement, the logo, the number of option columns, how many pages per student, or whether the roll grid is write-in or pre-bubbled, until after a generation has been spent.
findings.why_it_hurts: Every decision on this page (branding on/off, logo position left/center/right, shuffle) is invisible until it has consumed one of 5 daily generations and a stack of paper. Combined with the pre-bubbled roll bug and the branding-inherit bug above, a preview would have caught both before printing. The logo position segmented control in particular is meaningless without seeing the header.
findings.fix: Add a "Preview one sheet" button that renders the first selected student's sheet server-side and shows it inline (an of page 1 or an embedded PDF), without creating OmrSheet rows and without counting against the generation quota. Refresh it whenever branding, shuffle or roster changes.

findings.title: No way to reprint one student's sheet; a lost or torn sheet forces a full regeneration
findings.observed: The only outputs are whole-batch PDFs. OmrSheetSerializer already exposes a per-sheet pdf_url and a per-sheet question_paper_url (/api/v1/omr/sheets/<pk>/question-paper/), and OmrSheetQuestionPaperView implements it, but no frontend file references either — grep for question_paper_url and pdf_url across /frontend/src returns only the batch fields. There is no sheet list UI at all.
findings.why_it_hurts: A student arrives late, a sheet tears, a printer jams on page 23. The teacher's only recourse is to go back to the Generate page, uncheck 39 students, and burn another daily generation, or reprint the entire 40-page batch. For a coaching institute running weekly tests for 300 students across multiple staff, this is a daily occurrence.
findings.fix: Render the generated sheets as a list on this page (student, roll, sheet code, page count) with a per-row "Print sheet" and "Print packet" action hitting the existing per-sheet endpoints. Reprinting an existing sheet must not consume a generation, since no new sheet is created.

findings.title: The generated sheet wastes ~78% of every A4 page and carries no student instructions
findings.route: Generated PDF from /tests/:testId/sheets (inspected batch PDFs at 110 dpi)
findings.observed: A 10-question sheet uses a single narrow column in the top-left corner; roughly the bottom three quarters and right two thirds of the A4 page are blank. The layout is fixed at 25 rows per column, 2 columns, 50 questions per page, with no compaction for short tests and no option to place 2 students per page. The sheet also contains no instructions whatsoever: no "fill the bubble completely with a blue or black ball pen", no "do not fold or tear", no "do not make stray marks", no marks scheme, no date, no duration, no invigilator signature box, and no "Page 1 of 1". Option bubbles are 4.6mm across on a 5.6mm pitch, leaving only a 1mm gap between adjacent choices.
findings.why_it_hurts: A coaching institute running weekly 10 to 25 question tests for 300 students burns one full A4 per student where a half page would do; that is 150 wasted sheets a week and real money. The missing instruction block is worse: students tick, cross, circle or half-shade bubbles because nobody told them not to, and those reads land in the review queue or grade wrong. The 1mm inter-bubble gap makes an over-filled bubble bleed into its neighbour and read as a multi-mark.
findings.fix: Add a compact layout that packs short tests into the top half of the page (or 2 students per A4 with a cut line), selectable on the Generate page with a preview. Add a fixed instructions block and a signature/date row in the currently empty lower area of page 1. Widen OPTION_PITCH so the gap between bubbles is at least the bubble radius.

findings.title: Competitive / sectional mode is fully built in the backend and sold on the pricing page, but unreachable from the UI
findings.route: Test creation wizard (/classes/:id → new test) and /tests/:testId/sheets
findings.observed: Test.MODE_CHOICES contains competitive ("Competitive (Sections)"), Section and SectionMarkingScheme models exist, /api/v1/sections/ is routed, GenerateView builds sections_for_descriptor for competitive tests, build_template renders a sections block, and ExamOverview.jsx has a MODE_LABELS entry `competitive: "Competitive"`. But TestWizard.jsx's RadioGroup offers only "standard" and "roster_prebubbled" — grep for "competitive" across /frontend/src returns hits only in landing, Pricing, FAQ, Features, BuiltForPage and Footer. Pricing.jsx lists "Competitive / sectional papers" as available on all four plans and FAQ says the mode is chosen when you create the test.
findings.why_it_hurts: The coaching-institute persona is the one the marketing copy targets, and the single feature they were sold (NEET/UPSC style sectional papers with per-section choose-k policies) cannot be turned on. They pay, create a test, and find only two modes in the wizard. That is a refund conversation, not a usability nit.
findings.fix: Either surface competitive mode in the test wizard with a section builder (label, question range, policy, choose-k) and show the section legend on the Generate page so the teacher can confirm before printing, or remove the claim from Pricing, FAQ, Features and the landing pages until it ships.

findings.title: The batch answer-sheet PDF with every student's name is served from /media/ with no authentication
findings.observed: The success panel's download link is http://localhost:8000/media/omr_batches/<test-uuid>-<random-hex>.pdf. Fetched with curl, no cookie and no Authorization header: HTTP 200, 72935 bytes, containing all 7 students' full names and sheet codes. The code in GenerateView explicitly recognises the risk for the *question paper* batch ("This is a multi-student PII document, so it is served ONLY here (auth + owner/org scope), never via /media/") and routes it through an authenticated endpoint, but the answer-sheet batch is written straight to default_storage and handed out as a raw /media/ URL. Per-sheet pdf_file URLs have the same exposure.
findings.why_it_hurts: The URL ends up in browser history, in the download list, and in any "share this with the front desk" message. Anyone who obtains it (or scans /media/omr_batches/) gets a roster of student names for a test, plus the sheet codes that the scanner keys on. For a multi-staff coaching institute whose selling point is that staff cannot see each other's data, an unauthenticated media path defeats the whole scoping model.
findings.fix: Serve the batch through an authenticated, scope-checked endpoint exactly like OmrTestQuestionPapersBatchView, and return that endpoint's URL as batch_pdf_url. Do the same for per-sheet pdf_file. Have the frontend fetch it with downloadAuthedBlob, which already exists in api/omr.js.

findings.title: Regenerating silently overwrites the stored answer key of sheets that may already be printed and scanned
findings.observed: GenerateView does OmrSheet.objects.update_or_create(test, student, defaults={... 'question_order', 'option_order', 'answer_key', 'template_descriptor' ...}). Nothing checks whether the sheet already has scans or results attached, and the UI gives no warning at all: the second generation on my test simply reported "Generated 10 sheet(s)". If the teacher edited a question or an option between the first print and the regenerate, every already-printed sheet's stored key is rewritten to a key that no longer describes the paper in the student's hand.
findings.why_it_hurts: The product's core trust claim is that each sheet is graded against its own stored answer key. A teacher who reprints one lost sheet, or who fixes a typo in a question and regenerates, quietly invalidates the key for the whole batch, and the resulting marks are wrong with no error and no audit trail. Nobody will suspect the Generate page.
findings.fix: Before overwriting, detect whether any selected sheet already has a ScanJob or StudentResult, and if so show a modal: "3 of these sheets have already been scanned. Regenerating will replace their answer keys and previously printed sheets will no longer grade correctly." Offer "regenerate anyway" versus "reprint the existing sheets". Ideally version the sheet (bump a revision, keep the old key) instead of mutating it in place.

findings.title: Every roster on a class shows the same label in the picker, so you cannot tell them apart
findings.route: /tests/518bfa09-7aeb-485d-81e0-d3be1dfef189/sheets → Roster dropdown, after creating a second roster ("Evening batch") on the same class
findings.observed: The dropdown listed two entries, both reading exactly "Batch A". The roster's own name is discarded: rosterLabel(r) returns `${topClassName}` or `${topClassName} · ${section}` and never uses r.name. No student count is shown either. Selecting one and then the other silently swaps the student list underneath with no indication of which is which.
findings.why_it_hurts: A coaching institute keeps a morning batch and an evening batch on the same course, and a school keeps last term's roster alongside this term's. The teacher picks one at random, generates, prints, and discovers at distribution time that half the names are wrong. Since generations are rate limited, the retry costs quota as well as paper.
findings.fix: Label each option with the roster's own name plus the class/section context and the student count: "Evening batch · Batch A · 24 students". Fall back to the class name only when the roster is unnamed.

findings.title: The Generate page never repeats the "answer key incomplete" warning shown one screen earlier
findings.observed: The exam overview shows a prominent amber banner: "Some questions have no correct answer set, grading will skip them. Fix the answer key". One click later, the Generate page shows no warning at all and lets you generate and print the full batch. The server also accepts it without comment.
findings.why_it_hurts: The banner is exactly one click away from being forgotten, and the Generate page is the point of no return: after this, 40 sheets are printed and handed out. Questions with no key silently score zero for the whole class, which surfaces only in analytics days later and looks like the grading engine is broken.
findings.fix: Re-surface the same warning on the Generate page, above the Generate button, with the count ("3 of 10 questions have no correct answer and will be skipped") and a "Fix the answer key" link. Consider requiring an explicit confirmation modal to generate an exam with an incomplete key.

findings.title: Options per question and question-paper emission exist in the API but cannot be set from the UI
findings.observed: GenerateSerializer accepts emit_question_paper, but the frontend never sends it; it is only forced true as a side effect of shuffling, so with both shuffle toggles off there is no question paper produced and no way to ask for one. Test.default_options (which controls how many option columns are laid out, clamped 2..6) is exposed in the assessments serializer and honoured by GenerateView, but grep for default_options across /frontend/src returns nothing. Meanwhile FAQ.jsx and Features.jsx advertise "4 or 5 options" as a sheet-level choice.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher running an unshuffled test still wants a printed question paper from the system rather than maintaining a separate Word file, and cannot get one. A teacher who wants a uniform 5-column layout (so a spare option column exists for later questions) must instead add a fifth option to every single question by hand in the question editor. The advertised "4 or 5 options" setting does not exist as a setting.
findings.fix: Add an "Also print question papers" switch on the Generate page, forced on and locked when shuffle is on, and pass emit_question_paper. Add an "Options per question" segmented control (4 / 5 / 6) bound to default_options, with a note that questions carrying more options widen the sheet automatically.

findings.title: Test mode is invisible on the Generate page and cannot be changed after creation
findings.observed: The Generate page's body text contains no mention of the mode; asserted programmatically that the rendered text does not contain "re-bubbl". Only the exam overview shows a MODE tile. There is also no edit path: the mode radio group lives only in TestWizard.jsx and there is no test settings screen (routes/exam/ contains only ExamOverview.jsx and ExamQuestions.jsx).
findings.why_it_hurts: Whether the roll grid arrives pre-filled or blank changes what the teacher must tell students to do before the exam starts, and it is decided on a screen they saw days ago. If they picked wrong, the only fix is to delete the test and rebuild it with its questions and answer key.
findings.fix: Show the mode as a labelled read-only row in the "Generate & print" card ("Roll numbers: pre-printed for each student" or "Roll numbers: students bubble their own"), with a link to change it, and allow mode to be edited on a test that has no generated sheets yet.

findings.title: Small predictability and polish gaps on the Generate page
findings.observed: (a) With everyone selected the button reads "Generate sheets" and drops the count, so the one case where the number matters most (all 40) is the one case it is hidden. (b) The success toast reads "Generated 7 sheet(s)" with a parenthesised plural. (c) The print packet downloads as "question-papers.pdf" even though the button promises questions plus sheets. (d) "Download sheets PDF" is a plain anchor with target=_blank and no download attribute, so it opens a viewer rather than downloading, and the suggested filename is a raw uuid. (e) Nothing states the total page count or paper size before or after generating. (f) At 320px the h1 truncates to "Generate O…" while a full-width "Back to class" button keeps its room, and the 40-student list sits in a 224px nested scroll box with no search or roll-range filter, under a fixed bottom nav bar.
findings.why_it_hurts: Individually trivial, collectively they mean the teacher cannot answer "what exactly am I about to print, and how many pages" at any point in the flow, and on a phone they scroll a tiny inner box to find student 37.
findings.fix: Always show the count on the button ("Generate 40 sheets"). Pluralise properly. Name the packet file after the test. Use downloadAuthedBlob with a readable filename for the sheets PDF. Show "40 sheets · 40 pages · A4" next to the button and in the success panel. On mobile, let the student list grow with the page instead of nesting a scroll region, and add a name/roll filter once a roster exceeds about 15 students.

area: QR code + physical OMR sheet design (backend/omr generator, geometry, scan alignment)
worked: On a clean flatbed-style scan the sheet is genuinely solid: 50/50 correct at 130-400 DPI, perspective distortion up to 12% is fully corrected, and the fill reader is forgiving of real student behaviour (ticks, crosses, half-fills, scribbles, 1mm off-centre marks and 1.5mm ink halos all read correctly without bleeding into neighbours), and uniform print scaling ("fit to page") is self-correcting because the warp is fiducial-relative.

findings.title: Scanning is dead on this deployment: the QR decoder's native library is not installed
findings.observed: `from omr.scan.pipeline import process_scan_job` raises `ImportError: Unable to find zbar shared library`. pyzbar==0.1.9 is in requirements.txt but libzbar0 is a system package and is absent from this machine (`ldconfig -p | grep zbar` and a filesystem-wide `find libzbar*` both return nothing). The import is lazy inside `process_scan_job_task`, so generation and the UI look healthy and the failure only surfaces the moment a teacher uploads a scan. There is no fallback decoder (OpenCV ships `cv2.QRCodeDetector` and cv2 is already a dependency), and no doc or setup script lists the system package. The project's own Phase 0 plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-17-omrflow-phase0-foundations.md:732) predicted this exact failure and said STOP if it happened.
findings.why_it_hurts: The QR is the entire trust anchor. A teacher prints 40 sheets, runs the exam, photographs the stack, and every single job errors out. There is no manual-entry path to recover; the whole product stops at the last step of the workflow.
findings.fix: Add libzbar0 to a documented system-dependency list plus the deploy image, and add a startup healthcheck that fails loudly if pyzbar cannot load. Independently, add a `cv2.QRCodeDetector().detectAndDecode()` fallback inside `decode_qr` so a missing native lib degrades to slower decoding instead of a hard 500.

findings.title: A sheet placed upside down is silently graded as near-zero with 96% reported confidence
findings.observed: I rotated a fully-answered 50-question scan by 180 degrees and ran the real pipeline: QR decodes fine (decoders are rotation-invariant), all 4 fiducials are found, warp succeeds, and the result is 1/50 correct, 48 blank, roll read as '???' — with only 2 questions flagged, so pipeline.py:265 computes confidence = 0.96. The 4 fiducials are 4 identical 24px solid squares (geometry.py:_fiducials), so the corner set is 180-degree symmetric and carries zero orientation information; `detect_fiducials` just assigns blobs to image corners TL/TR/BL/BR and warps them onto the canonical TL/TR/BL/BR. The QR's known top-right position and its own orientation are decoded but never used to verify orientation. 90-degree rotation gives 0/50.
findings.why_it_hurts: Upside-down is the single most common handling error with a stack of loose sheets and a phone. The teacher gets a confident zero for a student who answered everything, with no flag telling her anything is wrong. One silent wrong score destroys trust in every other score on the page.
findings.fix: Break the fiducial symmetry (e.g. make the top-left marker a distinct shape/size, or add an L-shaped or double marker on one edge) so the corner set is orientation-unique. Additionally, cheap and immediate: after warping, re-run QR detection on the canonical image and assert the code's bounding box lands inside the descriptor's `qr` rect; if it lands in the opposite corner, rotate 180 and re-warp, and if it lands anywhere else, flag `alignment` instead of grading.

findings.title: A damaged, stapled or faded corner makes the reader pick an answer bubble as a fiducial and produce a believable wrong score
findings.observed: The candidate filter accepts any blob with area in [0.20x, 6.0x] of the fiducial, aspect within ±0.5 and solidity ≥0.60. A printed answer-bubble outline (r=9px) has area 254 vs expected 576 (ratio 0.44), aspect 1.0, solidity 0.78 — so every one of the 200+ bubbles on the page is a valid fiducial candidate, as are the QR's three finder patterns. There is no check that the 4 chosen points form a plausible A4 rectangle. Measured on real renders: covering the top-left fiducial (staple or correction fluid) makes it pick a roll-grid bubble at (219,375) → 4/50 correct; a torn bottom-right corner → 1/50 correct; a merely faded top-right fiducial (light toner) makes it pick the QR's finder pattern → 42/50 correct with 20 flags. In every case `detect_fiducials` returns success and no `alignment` review item is raised.
findings.why_it_hurts: The 42/50 case is the dangerous one: it looks like a normal score with a few review flags, so a teacher clears the flags and publishes a wrong result. Staples go in exactly the corner where the top-left fiducial sits, and low toner on the last 200 sheets of a print run is routine.
findings.fix: After picking 4 candidates, validate the geometry before warping: check the two horizontal spans and two vertical spans agree within ~5%, and that the width:height ratio matches the descriptor's (827:1169) within tolerance. Reject and flag `alignment` otherwise. Also tighten the candidate filter — require solidity ≥0.85 and area within [0.6x, 1.8x] so a hollow bubble outline cannot qualify — and print the fiducials larger with a guaranteed white quiet zone.

findings.title: Any phone photo taken on a desk fails alignment 100% of the time (global Otsu locks onto the page edge, not the ink)
findings.route: POST /api/v1/omr/scan/ → backend/omr/scan/align.py:124 (`cv2.THRESH_OTSU` over the whole frame)
findings.observed: I composited the real rendered sheet onto a background and swept the background brightness. With a pure-white background Otsu picks threshold 137 and fiducials are found. As soon as the surround is grey 200 or darker — i.e. any wooden desk, laminate table, notebook, floor or even a lightly shaded white table — Otsu jumps to threshold 206-222, the entire background becomes 'ink', the fiducials dissolve into one giant blob and detection fails. Result: 0/6 of my simulated desk-photo scenes (plain desk, desk with dark objects, 7-degree rotation, rotation + perspective, shadow, upside-down) got past stage 2. A separate test with a 45% brightness gradient across the page (hand shadow / window light) did get past alignment but then read 6/50 correct, because `to_binary` in scan/read.py uses the same global Otsu.
findings.why_it_hurts: The stated primary user 'uses a phone camera not a scanner'. Photographing a sheet on a desk is the default action, and it fails every time with a generic 'alignment' review item that gives the teacher no idea what to change. This alone would make a school abandon the product on day one.
findings.fix: Crop to the page before thresholding: find the largest quadrilateral contour (the sheet against the desk), warp to that, then threshold. Add a printed thin border rectangle just inside the margin on every page so this crop is reliable. Replace both global Otsu calls with `cv2.adaptiveThreshold` (or per-tile Otsu) so a shadow across half the page cannot swamp the histogram. Add explicit guidance in the scan UI and a rejection message that names the actual cause ("place the sheet on a plain light surface").

findings.title: The option letter is printed inside each bubble, consuming almost the entire 'empty bubble' budget and flooding the review queue
findings.observed: The A/B/C/D glyph is drawn at the bubble centre, inside the r*0.6 inner disc that `bubble_fill_ratio` samples. Measured on the real generated PDF: an untouched answer bubble already reads 0.148-0.196 fill against a FILL_LOW threshold of 0.20, i.e. the printing alone uses 74-98% of the entire 'empty' budget. Roll-grid bubbles, which have no letter inside, read exactly 0.000. Consequence at realistic capture resolutions: at 160 DPI 26 of 150 unmarked bubbles cross FILL_LOW, at 130 DPI 18 cross it, at 100 DPI 75 of 150 cross it. Each crossing sets the question's flag to `faint`, so on a clean synthetic scan with no student error at all, half the questions on the sheet route to review.
findings.why_it_hurts: The coaching-institute owner with 300 students a week is the person who cares about throughput; a design that manufactures dozens of spurious review items per sheet from the printing itself makes the review queue useless and the confidence score meaningless. It also means real toner spread, a slightly dark photocopy, or JPEG sharpening pushes clean sheets over the edge.
findings.fix: Move the option letter outside the circle (a small letter above the column, or immediately left of the bubble), so an unmarked bubble reads ~0.00 like the roll grid does. That restores the full 0-0.20 band as genuine headroom. If the letter must stay inside, print it in a light grey (e.g. 40% K) and mask the glyph region out of the sampled disc, and raise FILL_LOW well above the measured print baseline.

findings.title: The sheet carries no instructions to the student at all
findings.route: backend/omr/generator.py:render_sheet_pdf — the draw passes are branding, header, roll grid, answer bubbles, section legend; there is no instruction pass
findings.observed: Every generated sheet I inspected (including the real one at backend/media/omr_sheets/omr_sheets/22e60ebe-6SFKCJFN.pdf) contains only: test title, Name, Sheet ID, 'Roll No.' and the grids. Nothing tells a student to use black or blue ballpoint, to fill the bubble completely rather than tick it, to mark only one option, not to write in the margins, not to fold or staple the sheet, and not to erase (there is no erasure-tolerant handling). Meanwhile the top-right two-thirds of page 1 (roughly x 200-790, y 170-400) is completely blank whitespace.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher handing these to 40 fourteen-year-olds has to read the rules aloud every time, and any student who ticks in the wrong place, folds a corner or staples the stack corrupts a fiducial. The blank space that should carry the instructions is the same space currently going to waste.
findings.fix: Add a boxed instruction block in the empty right half of the header band on page 1, and a one-line footer on every page. Suggested content: fill the bubble completely in black or blue ballpoint; mark only one option per question; do not tick, cross or write outside the bubbles; do not fold, staple or tear the corners; keep the black corner squares and the code square clean.

findings.title: The roll number is machine-only: nothing on the sheet lets a human read it, and the grid's own labelling is ambiguous
findings.route: backend/omr/generator.py:_draw_roll_grid + backend/omr/views.py:376 (sheet_dict has no printed roll field)
findings.observed: Three separate problems in one block. (a) The roll number is never printed as text: the header prints test title, Name and Sheet ID only, so in prebubbled mode a teacher sorting 40 sheets must decode the shaded grid by eye, and in write-in mode a student has no printed number to copy. (b) The digit-column headers are drawn as 0,1,2,... (the digit *place index*, generator.py:516) directly above rows labelled 0-9 (the digit *value*) — a student with roll 7 has no way to know whether to shade column 0 or column 2, and no leading-zero instruction exists. There are also no write-in boxes above the grid to write the number in figures first, which is the universal OMR convention. (c) The 'Roll No.' label baseline sits at y=166px, 1px above the column-header glyph tops at y=167, and extends horizontally right across the '0' and '1' headers — in the rendered PDF they visibly collide. (d) write-in is the DEFAULT roll_kind, and I verified that a blank roll grid returns `('???', 'roll_unreadable')`, which pipeline.py turns into a ReviewItem — so every sheet where a student did not shade the grid generates a review item, even though identity already came from the QR and the roll is not used for grading in that mode.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher's most basic physical task, sorting a stack back into roll order, is impossible by eye. Students mis-shade the grid because the columns are unlabelled in any meaningful way, and the default mode then generates one review item per sheet for a field nobody needed.
findings.fix: Print the roll number in figures next to the grid (and a row of write-in boxes above it in write-in mode), label the columns as place values or leave them blank rather than 0/1/2, add 'write your roll number and shade the matching bubble in each column' to the instruction block, move the 'Roll No.' label up so it clears the column headers, and stop raising `roll_unreadable` when roll_kind is writein and the grid is entirely blank.

findings.title: Pages 2 and beyond carry no human-readable identity at all
findings.route: backend/omr/generator.py:759 (`if page_no == 0:` gates branding, header and roll grid)
findings.observed: I generated a 100-question sheet and looked at page 2: it has 4 fiducials, a QR, and 50 rows of bubbles. No student name, no Sheet ID text, no roll number, no test title, no 'Page 2 of 2'. The `page|total` information exists only inside the QR payload.
findings.why_it_hurts: A stack of 40 two-page sheets that gets knocked over cannot be re-paired by a human at all — the teacher's only option is to feed everything back through the scanner and hope. If one page 2 goes missing, she has no way to tell whose it was.
findings.fix: Repeat a compact identity strip on every page: student name, Sheet ID, and 'Page N of M' in plain text, placed in the top-left area below the fiducial where there is already free space.

findings.title: Roughly half of every sheet is blank, capping the layout at 50 questions per page and doubling print cost past Q50
findings.observed: On page 1 the two answer columns sit at x 71-137 and 444-510; everything right of x~520 is blank for the full page height, and the band from y 170-400 is blank across the right two-thirds. On page 2, questions end at y≈751 of 1169 because `row_pitch` is forced to page 1's constrained value (28px) while page 2's content starts at y=79 — the bottom 35% of page 2 is empty. ANSWERS_PER_PAGE is hard-coded to 2 columns × 25 rows = 50. With bubbles 4.57mm across and a 5.59mm option pitch, four columns of 30 rows would fit comfortably on the same A4.
findings.why_it_hurts: A 100-question test needs 2 sheets instead of 1. For the coaching institute running weekly tests for 300 students that is 300 extra printed pages, 300 extra scans, 300 extra chances for a page to go missing, and a `missing_page` review item every time one does. It is also the reason the instruction block and the identity strip 'have nowhere to go'.
findings.fix: Use the full page width (3-4 answer columns), let page 2+ compute its own row pitch instead of inheriting page 1's, and move the roll grid beside the header rather than below it. Reclaim the freed header space for instructions.

findings.title: A long institution heading prints straight over the top-right fiducial and off the page edge
findings.observed: The heading is truncated by character count, never by measured width, and is drawn at 12pt Helvetica-Bold from x=76px with no clipping. Model max_length is 255, so the UI accepts far more than the generator can fit. Measured with reportlab's own `stringWidth`: a 65-character all-caps heading is 650pt wide and reaches x=978px on an 827px page; a realistic 87-character school name ('SHRI GURU NANAK PUBLIC SENIOR SECONDARY SCHOOL, SECTOR 45 AND JUNIOR COLLEGE OF SCIENCE') reaches x=737px. The QR block starts at x=707 and the top-right fiducial spans x 763-787. I rendered it and confirmed the text prints through the fiducial square and runs off the sheet.
findings.why_it_hurts: An org admin types their real school name once, and every sheet that org ever prints has a corrupted top-right fiducial — which, per the fiducial finding above, does not fail cleanly but silently picks the QR finder pattern instead and produces plausible wrong scores. The cause is invisible to the user.
findings.fix: Measure with `stringWidth` and shrink-to-fit or ellipsize at the real BRAND_X_RIGHT=700px boundary, and enforce the same limit in the serializer with a character/width warning shown in the branding settings UI so the admin sees the truncation before printing 300 sheets.

findings.title: The QR is small enough that a photocopy or a slightly out-of-focus phone shot kills it outright
findings.observed: Payload 'fc207ef7-ABCD2345|1|1' is 21 bytes → QR version 2, 25 modules, plus a 4-module quiet zone inside the same 80px box = 33 modules across 20.3mm. That is a 15.4mm code at 0.616mm per module. Measured decode results: clean scans at 130-400 DPI decode fine, JPEG q40 decodes fine, but a simulated photocopy (contrast 0.6, blur, noise) FAILS, a second-generation washed-out photocopy FAILS, and a 3px defocus blur FAILS. The QR also sits only 4px below the top-right fiducial square, so a 6.1mm solid black square intrudes into the quiet-zone neighbourhood. There is exactly one QR per page and no alternative machine-readable code.
findings.why_it_hurts: Teachers photocopy, and phone autofocus misses on a flat white page more often than anyone admits. When the QR dies the sheet cannot even be identified, so it lands in review as `no_qr` with no student attached — the teacher must match it to a name by hand. A torn or coffee-stained top-right corner has the same effect.
findings.fix: Enlarge the QR to ~28-30mm (module ≥0.9mm), raise error correction from M to Q or H, and increase the gap to the top-right fiducial. Consider a second QR in the bottom-left corner so one damaged corner is survivable, and make sure the review UI lets the teacher type the printed 8-character Sheet ID (which is already on page 1) to recover a no_qr sheet.

findings.title: The wrong-test upload guard is dead code because the sheet code prefix can never parse as a UUID
findings.observed: `make_sheet_code` builds the code as the first 8 hex chars of the test UUID plus a token (e.g. `22e60ebe-6SFKCJFN`, confirmed against a real generated sheet in media). `_parse_test_id_from_sheet_code` does `uuid.UUID(hex=prefix)` on those 8 chars, which always raises ValueError and returns None, so the `test_mismatch` branch at pipeline.py:205 is unreachable for every sheet the product has ever produced. Its own docstring still describes the old `{test_id:06d}-{token}` format. The fallback path returns `sheet_not_found:22e60ebe-6SFKCJFN` as a raw job failure string rather than the intended `test_mismatch` review item.
findings.why_it_hurts: Mixing last week's sheets into this week's scan batch is a routine mistake in a school office. Instead of a clear 'this sheet belongs to a different test' review item, the teacher gets a job marked FAILED with an opaque code string and no guidance, and the failure is a hard failure rather than something the review queue can resolve.
findings.fix: Compare the 8-hex prefix as a string against `str(job.batch.test_id).replace('-','')[:8]` instead of parsing it as a UUID, and keep the `test_mismatch` review reason. Also treat prefix-match-but-sheet-not-found as a review item rather than a hard job failure.

findings.title: With branding on, the header lines are crushed together and descenders collide with the line below
findings.route: Org settings → default_sheet_heading set → generated sheet page 1 header (backend/omr/generator.py:_draw_header, branding branch, lines 440-468)
findings.observed: When branding is active the code drops the institution line, then squeezes the remaining 4 lines into the gap between the branding band and the fixed roll-grid label by shrinking leading to as little as MIN_LEADING=7px and font size to `leading_px - 1`. I rendered it: 'Midterm Physics' / 'Subject: Physics' / 'Name: Aarav Sharma' / 'Sheet ID: ABCD2345' print with effectively zero leading and the descenders of one line touch the caps of the next.
findings.why_it_hurts: Branding is the path every paying org will use, so the crushed, unprofessional header is what schools actually hand to students and parents. It also makes the student name harder to read at a glance when sorting.
findings.fix: The real cause is that the roll grid's y position is hard-coded (HEADER_H=168) so the header has nowhere to expand. Make the roll-grid origin a function of the actual header height instead of a constant, so branding pushes the whole block down rather than compressing the text.

findings.title: The institution name is hard-coded to empty on every generated sheet
findings.observed: `_draw_header` supports an institution line and the PRD (prompts/PRD.md:61) says each sheet carries an 'institution/test header', but the generation view passes an empty string unconditionally. Verified on the real sheet in media: it starts with 'Unit Test 1' and no school name. The only way to get a school name onto a sheet is the separate branding heading field, which most users will not find.
findings.why_it_hurts: Sheets that leave the building with no school name on them look unofficial to parents and are hard to identify if they get mixed with another institution's papers during a joint exam.
findings.fix: Populate `institution` from the active organisation's name (falling back to the user's account name) so the default output is correct without the admin having to discover the branding settings.

area: Scan upload path, results board, review queue and sheet corrector
worked: The scan results board is the right shape: flagged-first ordering, an All / Needs attention filter, a per-sheet card with student name and score, and an inline corrector that correctly pre-fills the actual detected marks and correctly recomputes the score on save (the bubble-geometry overlay data is all plumbed through and renders 40 correct circles).

findings.title: Re-scanning a sheet permanently destroys the score: every scan of the same sheet is UNIONed, never replaced
findings.route: /tests/8409ed44-4888-42e6-aae3-6006396adb61/scan → upload a sheet, then upload a second photo of the SAME sheet
findings.observed: I uploaded a sheet with all 10 bubbles filled exactly on the answer key. The API confirms that scan read the key perfectly (batch b1ce37eb, `THIS SCAN READ` == `answer_key`, 10/10). The stored StudentResult for that same sheet came back as **6.00 / 10.00**. Reason: `_maybe_grade()` collects `ScanJob.objects.filter(omr_sheet=omr_sheet, status__in=[DONE, NEEDS_REVIEW])` across ALL batches ever, then merges with `aggregated_reads[q_pos].extend(...)` — a union of every read from every scan. Divya Nambiar's stored responses after a clean scan plus a blurry re-photo are q0=['A','D'], q4=['C','B','A','D'], q5=['A','B','C','D'] and her score is 1.00/10.00 for a sheet she actually scored 8/10 on. The UI shows a plain number with no hint it is a merge, and re-photographing a bad scan makes the score strictly WORSE, never better.
findings.why_it_hurts: Re-photographing a sheet that came out blurry is the single most common thing a teacher does with a phone camera. Doing the obvious recovery action silently and permanently corrupts the student's grade, and there is no way to undo it or even to notice it. A coaching institute running weekly tests would publish wrong ranks every week.
findings.fix: Grade from ONE authoritative scan per (sheet, page), not the union. On a new ScanJob for a sheet+page that already has a job, supersede the old one (mark it `superseded`, exclude it from `_maybe_grade`) and show the teacher a card saying "This sheet was already scanned on <date> and scored X; the new scan scores Y. Keep new / keep old?" Never merge marked options across jobs.

findings.title: Resolving a review item writes the teacher's answer onto the WRONG question
findings.route: /tests/8409ed44-4888-42e6-aae3-6006396adb61/review → any card → pick a letter → Resolve
findings.observed: `ResolveReviewItemView` ignores which question the item is about and applies `marked_options` to `QuestionResponse.objects.filter(student_result=..., flagged=True).first()`. I resolved the item whose reason was **ALIGNMENT / FIDUCIALS NOT FOUND** (a whole-page geometry failure, nothing to do with any question) by picking "A" — exactly what the UI offers. Divya Nambiar's **question 1** was silently overwritten to `marked_options: ['A']`, `is_correct: false`, `flagged: false`. Her real answer to Q1 is gone. The same happens for `no_qr`, `roll_unreadable` and `missing_page` items. For sheets with several double_mark flags, every item displays the same question (`get_q_pos` also returns "the first flagged response") so three flags resolved in sequence land on questions 1, 2, 3 in flag order rather than on the questions the teacher was shown.
findings.why_it_hurts: The review queue is sold as the safety net that guarantees nothing is guessed. It is in fact the component that fabricates answers. A teacher clearing 18 flags to publish results is silently rewriting a different student answer on each click, and the resulting score looks completely normal.
findings.fix: Persist `question`/`q_pos` on the ReviewItem at creation time in `_create_review_item` (the pipeline already knows the q_pos of every flagged read), have the serializer return that stored value, and make resolve target `QuestionResponse.objects.get(student_result=..., q_pos=review_item.q_pos)` — 400 if it does not match. For sheet-level reasons (no_qr, alignment, roll_unreadable, missing_page, test_mismatch) do not show an answer picker at all; offer the actions that actually fix them (re-upload this page, reassign student, discard).

findings.title: Light pencil marks are read as blank, flagged as nothing, and reported with 100% confidence
findings.observed: I scanned a sheet with all 10 correct bubbles filled in a light grey (a realistic soft pencil). Every question came back `{"marked": [], "flag": null}`, job `confidence: 1.0`, and the board rendered a green **CLEAN** badge for "Sneha Pillai" with a score of **0 / 10**. `to_binary` uses global Otsu, so a page dominated by black print and a QR block sets a threshold that classifies a light pencil as paper — the fill ratio lands at 0.0, which is below `FILL_LOW` (0.20), so it is not even ambiguous enough to raise the existing `faint` flag.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the worst possible failure: a student who did everything right gets a zero, and the product actively tells the teacher it is clean and 100% confident. Nothing in the UI would ever make a teacher look at that sheet. A whole class of soft-pencil users is silently zeroed.
findings.fix: Replace global Otsu with adaptive/local thresholding (`cv2.adaptiveThreshold`) or normalise each bubble against its own local paper patch, so mark darkness is measured relative to nearby paper rather than to the QR block. Additionally, when an entire page reads as zero marks, always flag it `all_blank` for review rather than reporting confidence 1.0 — a completely empty sheet is a scan problem far more often than a genuine result.

findings.title: The review queue never shows the bubble, the sheet, or the student — a teacher cannot possibly decide
findings.observed: 22 identical cards. Each one shows a red reason chip, two lines that both read "Sheet:" (one is the human code `8409ed44-WH7AKMCB`, the other a raw UUID `c5fc2107-d119-4d6f-be2b-19d9b3f3bfb6`), sometimes `Q0`, then "Mark correct answer(s): A B C D E" and a Resolve button. There is no image of the bubble, no thumbnail of the sheet, no student name, no link to the sheet or to the corrector, and no way to skip, discard or bulk-handle an item. The four `no_qr` items have no sheet code at all — no student, no filename, no page number — so there is literally no information identifying which piece of paper failed.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher is asked to decide what a student marked while being shown nothing at all about what the student marked. The only rational behaviours are to guess or to abandon the queue, and guessing is what the queue exists to prevent. On mobile each card is ~490px tall, so 22 items is 11,000px of scrolling through indistinguishable grey boxes.
findings.fix: Every card must carry: student name and roll, exam name, the printed question number, and a cropped image of that question's bubble row taken from the warped scan (the endpoint `/omr/scan-jobs/<id>/warped/` and `bubble_geometry` already exist — crop server-side or draw a clipped canvas client-side). Add a "View whole sheet" link into the corrector. For orphan `no_qr` items show the original uploaded filename and a thumbnail of the raw upload so the teacher knows which paper to re-shoot.

findings.title: The sheet corrector renders the scanned sheet 72 pixels wide on desktop
findings.observed: The corrector dialog opens at ~385px total width because `DialogContent` is capped at `sm:max-w-sm`. `SheetCorrectorPanel` is written as `md:flex-row` with a fixed `w-72` (288px) control column and `flex-1` for the image, so the image column collapses. I measured the rendered ``: **71.98px wide** for an 827x1169 sheet. There is no zoom, no pan, no click-to-enlarge. The bubble overlay draws all 40 circles into that 72px strip. The flagged question is not highlighted anywhere in the 10-row grid; you find the double mark only by noticing two blue buttons on one row.
findings.why_it_hurts: The entire promise of the corrector is "look at the actual bubble and decide". At 72px the teacher can see nothing and can only accept whatever the machine read, which defeats the point of having a review step. On mobile the image is a usable 299px but sits in a separate scroll region above the grid, so you can never see the sheet and the answer you are changing at the same time.
findings.fix: Give the corrector its own wide dialog (`max-w-5xl` or a full-screen sheet on both breakpoints), keep the image at ≥55% of the width on desktop, and add zoom plus a "jump to flagged question" control that scrolls and highlights the flagged row and pans the image to that bubble row.

findings.title: Sheets that failed QR or alignment offer "Fix & re-grade", then dead-end with a developer error
findings.route: /tests/<id>/scan → upload a rotated / cropped / non-sheet image → click "Fix & re-grade" on the resulting card
findings.observed: A cropped sheet and a random photo both produced orange "NEEDS ATTENTION" cards reading "Unknown student · Roll: n/a · no_qr · n/a score" with a primary **Fix & re-grade** button. Clicking it opens a corrector titled "Correct sheet, Unknown student" showing "No sheet image available" and an answer grid with exactly one row (Q1). Pressing Save & re-grade produces the toast **"No sheet ID, cannot regrade"** and nothing else. A rotated phone photo produced an `alignment` card that displayed a score of 4/10 — a score borrowed from a different scan of the same sheet, since the alignment-failed job has no reads of its own.
findings.why_it_hurts: For exactly the failures where a teacher most needs to see what they photographed (upside down? cut off? wrong page?), the product shows no image at all, offers an action it cannot perform, and answers with a developer string. The teacher has no idea which of the 40 sheets on their desk to re-shoot, and an alignment-failed card showing a plausible score invites them to accept it.
findings.fix: Always persist and serve the ORIGINAL uploaded image (not only the warped canonical), and show it on failure cards with the original filename. Replace "Fix & re-grade" on these cards with "Re-upload this sheet" and "Assign to student manually". Replace the toast with a real explanation, e.g. "No QR code found. The sheet may be rotated, cropped or too blurry. Re-photograph the whole page with all four corner squares visible."

findings.title: "N of N sheet(s) processed successfully" is shown for sheets that completely failed, and for zero sheets
findings.route: /tests/<id>/scan → upload 7 files including a cropped sheet and a non-sheet photo; separately upload a corrupt PDF
findings.observed: With 2 of 7 files failing QR entirely, the banner read "**7 of 7 sheet(s) processed successfully**" above 5 cards marked "need attention". A deliberately corrupt PDF returns HTTP 201 `{"total":0,"processed":0}` (the view does `except Exception: continue` on PDF parse failure and silently drops the whole file), and the UI then renders "**0 of 0 sheet(s) processed successfully**" with an empty board — while still having consumed a ScanEvent against the monthly scan quota.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher scanning between periods reads the green tick and the word "successfully" and moves on. Whole exams can go ungraded because a 40-page PDF failed to parse and the app said it succeeded, and the scan quota is charged for the non-event.
findings.fix: Split the banner into "X graded · Y need attention · Z could not be read" and use a warning tone whenever Y+Z > 0. Return a per-file `skipped` list from `ScanUploadView` naming each file it could not open and why, render it above the board, and do not create the ScanEvent when `total == 0`.

findings.title: Unsupported image formats (iPhone HEIC) fail as "image_not_found", and one bad file can 500 the whole batch
findings.route: /tests/<id>/scan → upload a file the decoder cannot open
findings.observed: The input accepts `image/*,.pdf` with no client-side validation. A file OpenCV cannot decode produces a job with `status: failed`, `error_reason: "image_not_found"` — which is false, the image was found, it just was not decodable. That raw token is printed verbatim on the card. In the browser the same upload also returned a hard **HTTP 500 (Django ImportError debug page)** and the only feedback was a bare **"Upload failed"** toast that vanished after ~4 seconds, leaving the page exactly as before with no record of what went wrong. iPhones shoot HEIC by default and `accept="image/*"` lets them straight through.
findings.why_it_hurts: The brief's primary user photographs sheets on a phone. If those photos are HEIC, every single one fails with a message that means nothing, and the teacher has no way to learn that they need to change a camera setting. A single bad file taking down a 40-sheet batch means re-doing the whole upload with no clue which file to remove.
findings.fix: Validate extension and size in `DropZone` before upload and reject unsupported types inline with a named list ("HEIC is not supported yet, set your iPhone camera to Most Compatible or share as JPEG"). Server-side, wrap per-file decode in try/except so one bad file never aborts the batch, and replace `image_not_found` with a human reason (`could_not_read_image`). Make upload errors a persistent inline banner listing the offending filenames, not a 4-second toast.

findings.title: Saving a correction silently resolves every open flag on the sheet and paints the card green while still showing the red flag
findings.route: /tests/<id>/scan → "Fix & re-grade" → change one bubble → Save & re-grade
findings.observed: I fixed one double mark on Imran Sheikh's sheet. `OmrSheetRegradeView` runs `ReviewItem.objects.filter(omr_sheet=..., resolved=False).update(resolved=True)` — the sheet's unrelated `roll_unreadable` item was closed too, and the queue dropped from 21 to 19 items. The card then rendered a green **CLEAN** badge with the red text **double_mark** still underneath it, and the score reformatted from "2 / 10" to "2.00 / 10.00". `handleRegraded` hard-codes `status: "done", flags: []` regardless of what the server returns, so a sheet whose `needs_review` is still true is shown as clean. The same wholesale auto-resolve fires if a teacher opens a CLEAN sheet with the "Review" button and presses Save without changing anything.
findings.why_it_hurts: Fixing one thing marks everything on that sheet as verified, including identity problems the teacher never looked at. The contradictory Clean-badge-plus-red-flag card destroys confidence in every other badge on the page: a teacher who spots one lie stops trusting the green ticks.
findings.fix: Only resolve ReviewItems whose q_pos the teacher actually changed; leave sheet-level items (roll_unreadable, missing_page, roll_mismatch) open and tell the user "1 flag fixed, 1 identity flag still open". Drive the card state from the server response (`needs_review`, remaining flags) instead of hard-coding it, clear `error_reason` when clearing `flags`, and normalise the score format.

findings.title: Correcting a student roll silently attaches the sheet to any student in the account with that number, or silently does nothing
findings.route: /tests/<id>/scan → "Fix & re-grade" → "Student roll (correct if wrong)" → Save & re-grade
findings.observed: The corrector's roll field posts to `OmrSheetRegradeView`, which does `_Student.objects.filter(scope_filter(request, "roster__"), roll_number=new_roll).first()` — scoped to the whole account, not to this exam's roster or class, unordered, first match wins, and `if student is not None` with no else. The seeded account already has rolls 001-010 in Grade 10 and 101-105 in Grade 9 Science; a teacher with six classes will have a roll 5 in every one. Typing a roll that exists in another class reassigns the sheet and its score to that other class's student and reports "Sheet re-graded successfully". Typing a roll that exists nowhere does nothing at all and reports the same success.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher fixing a misread roll is deliberately reassigning a grade, which is the highest-stakes action in the product, and it is done blind: no confirmation of who the sheet is moving to, no error when it fails, no warning when the match is ambiguous. Marks land on the wrong child's report card and nobody finds out until a parent complains.
findings.fix: Restrict the roll lookup to the roster(s) attached to this test, resolve it as the teacher types and show the matched student's name for confirmation before Save, and return 400 "No student with roll <n> in <roster>" on no match and "Roll <n> matches N students, pick one" on ambiguity. Replace the free-text field with a searchable student picker sourced from the exam's roster.

findings.title: A sheet from the wrong exam is reported as the raw string "sheet_not_found:8409ed44-45TWYP4F" and never reaches the review queue
findings.route: Upload a sheet printed for exam A into exam B's scan page
findings.observed: The friendly `test_mismatch` path ("Wrong test, sheet belongs to a different test") is dead code. `_parse_test_id_from_sheet_code` does `uuid.UUID(hex=sheet_code.split("-")[0])` on a code of the form `8409ed44-45TWYP4F`; the prefix is only 8 hex characters, so it always raises and returns None, and the guard `if parsed_test_id is not None` never fires. Execution falls through to the OmrSheet lookup, which raises DoesNotExist, and the job is set to `status=failed`, `error_reason="sheet_not_found:8409ed44-45TWYP4F"` with **no ReviewItem created**. The card shows that raw string; the review queue never mentions it.
findings.why_it_hurts: Mixing up two piles of printed sheets is the single most likely physical mistake at a coaching institute with weekly tests across multiple batches. The one message the product has for this situation never shows, and the failure is invisible in the review queue, so a teacher just sees a smaller-than-expected number of results and no explanation.
findings.fix: Parse the full UUID (the code prefix is a truncated hex, so either store the full test UUID in the QR payload or look the sheet up globally by `sheet_code` and compare its `test_id` to the batch's). When they differ, set `test_mismatch`, create a ReviewItem, and show "This sheet belongs to <other exam name>. Scan it under that exam instead."

findings.title: Flags are dumped as raw machine tokens, twice, and never name a question number
findings.observed: One card read: chips `roll_unreadable` `faint` `faint` `double_mark` `double_mark` `double_mark` `double_mark` `double_mark`, and immediately below, the same content again as one red comma-joined string `roll_unreadable,faint,faint,double_mark,double_mark,double_mark,double_mark,double_mark`. No question numbers, no plain English, no deduplication, and the review queue shows `Q0` (a zero-indexed position) for questions the printed sheet numbers 1-10. The review queue also hardcodes options A-E and offers **E** on a sheet printed with only A-D.
findings.why_it_hurts: "double_mark ×5" tells a teacher there is a problem but not where it is, so they must open the corrector and hunt through the grid row by row. Offering E on a four-option paper lets a teacher record an answer the student could not physically have given. `Q0` sends them to the wrong question or convinces them the data is broken.
findings.fix: Render flags as deduplicated sentences with 1-based question numbers, e.g. "Two bubbles filled on Q3 and Q7", "Faint mark on Q5", "Roll number could not be read".
