Drop the duplicate `error_reason` line. Derive the option labels from the sheet's `template_descriptor` instead of hardcoding A-E, and display `q_pos + 1` everywhere the teacher sees a question.

findings.title: The scan results board exists only in page state: refresh or navigate away and it is gone forever
findings.observed: `batch` and `sheets` are React state only. There is no batch history route and `/api/v1/omr/scan-batches/` returns 404 (only `/scan-batches/<id>/` exists), so there is no way to list past uploads. Clicking "Results" or the browser back button loses the per-sheet board permanently — you can never return to "which of the 40 sheets I just uploaded need attention". The Results page and the exam Overview surface no pending-review count at all; with 22 open review items the Overview's Lifecycle panel showed only Edit questions / Generate & print / Scan sheets / Results / Analytics, with no Review step and no badge.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher uploading 40 sheets between periods gets one shot at triaging them. Any interruption, tab close, or accidental navigation and the triage list is unrecoverable; the only remaining signal is a scattered NEEDS REVIEW column on the Results table. Nothing anywhere warns that 22 flags are open before results are shared publicly.
findings.fix: Add a scan-batch history list per exam (`GET /omr/scan-batches/?test=`) and make `/tests/<id>/scan/batches/<batchId>` a real route so any board can be reopened. Put an open-review count badge on the Review nav item, on the exam Overview lifecycle, and as a blocking warning on the "Share results publicly" action.

findings.title: Upload is one long blocking request with no real progress and no cancel; the progress bar is dead code
findings.observed: Processing runs inside the POST (Celery eager), measured at ~0.36s per sheet, so 40 sheets is a ~15s blocking request and 300 sheets is ~110s. During all of it the only feedback is the button label changing to "Uploading…". The "Processing… X/Y sheets" block and `<Progress>` bar never render, because they are gated on `batch && !done` and `batch` is only set after the POST resolves, by which time processing is finished. There is no cancel, no per-file status, and no upload byte progress. Separately, `startPolling` only stops on `status === "done" || processed >= total`, so a batch that ends in a failed/error state polls forever, and on a network error it clears the interval and leaves the UI frozen at "Processing…" with only a toast and no retry.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher with 40 sheets stares at a dead button for 15 seconds with no idea whether it is working, and is very likely to click again or reload — which on reload loses the board entirely. At institute scale the request will hit a proxy timeout and the teacher will never see a result even though the sheets were graded.
findings.fix: Return the batch id immediately and process asynchronously so the existing polling and progress bar actually run; stream per-file status into the board as each sheet finishes ("12 of 40 · Asha Rao 8/10"). Add a hard poll timeout with a visible "Still processing / Retry" state, terminate polling on terminal error statuses, and add a cancel control.

findings.title: The corrector asks the teacher to "Mark correct bubbles per question" and never shows the answer key or which answers are right
findings.observed: The control column is labelled "Mark correct bubbles per question" above a grid pre-filled with what the scanner detected. The label reads as an instruction to enter the correct answers (the key), not to record what the student actually filled. Nothing in the panel shows the answer key, marks right/wrong, or previews the resulting score; the header shows only "Confidence: 90%" with no explanation of what that measures or what threshold matters. Save applies whatever is in the grid as the authoritative reads for the whole sheet with no confirmation step.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who reads the label the obvious way will tick the answer key and hand that student a perfect score, and the app will accept it silently. Even a teacher who reads it correctly has no way to sanity-check the outcome, because the score does not update until after the dialog closes.
findings.fix: Relabel to "What the student marked" and add a per-row key indicator (a small tick/cross against the answer key) plus a live "Score will change from 2/10 to 5/10" line above the Save button. Explain the confidence figure in a tooltip or replace it with the concrete count ("3 of 10 questions unclear").

findings.title: No scanning guidance anywhere, and "Camera (mobile)" is shown on desktop
findings.observed: The scan page is a title, a dashed drop zone reading "Drop sheet images or PDFs here", a "Camera (mobile)" button and "Upload & scan". There is no statement of supported formats, no size or file-count limit, no note that a PDF may hold many sheets, and no photography guidance (all four corner squares visible, flat, even light, one sheet per photo) even though every failure I produced was caused by exactly those things. The "Camera (mobile)" button renders on desktop where it just opens a file picker, and the "Upload & scan" button when disabled looks like a normal solid primary button with no explanation that a file is required.
findings.why_it_hurts: Every teacher's first upload is a guess, and the failure modes are all preventable with two lines of instruction. The parenthetical "(mobile)" on a desktop button reads like an unfinished feature.
findings.fix: Add a short always-visible checklist next to the drop zone ("JPG or PNG or PDF · all four corner squares in frame · one sheet per photo · flat and evenly lit") plus the accepted formats and any file-count limit. Hide the camera button when `capture` is unsupported and drop "(mobile)" from its label. Show "Select at least one file" beneath the disabled button.

findings.title: Raw UUIDs shown as page subtitles, and toasts cover the cards they describe
findings.observed: The review queue header reads "Test #8409ed44-4888-42e6-aae3-6006396adb61" and the Results page reads "Test #8409ed44-4888-42e6-aae3-6006396adb61" instead of "Weekly Test 1", even though the breadcrumb directly above already knows the title. On the scan board the "Scan started, 7 image(s) queued" toast sits over the fifth sheet card, hiding its score and its Fix button until it expires.
findings.why_it_hurts: A 36-character hex string as the page subtitle looks like a bug and gives a teacher juggling six classes nothing to confirm they are on the right exam. A toast that covers actionable cards makes people click the wrong row.
findings.fix: Fetch and display the exam title (the review route already has `testId`, and `ExamOverview` already loads the test). Position toasts so they never overlap the results list, or dismiss the "scan started" toast as soon as the board renders.

area: Results, Analytics, report cards, student detail, public result portal
worked: The Analytics "Questions" tab is the one genuinely good screen: real question text, colour-coded wrong-rate badges and a per-option bar chart with the key highlighted, all flat and gradient-free; the two-page report card PDF has the right skeleton (name, roll, score, percentile, class comparison, per-question, missed items) and CSV/Excel/PDF exports all download and contain correct data; the public lookup endpoint's access-code check is properly constant-time with no roll-existence oracle and is throttled.

findings.title: Public leaderboard leaks the whole class roster and scores with no access code and no roll number
findings.route: /tests/:id/results → "Share results publicly" → "Show public leaderboard" on; then GET /api/v1/public/r/<slug>/leaderboard/ anonymously
findings.observed: I published Unit Test 3 Chemistry, set Access mode to "Require an access code" and saved a code. POST /lookup/ without the code correctly returns 403 "Invalid access code." But GET /leaderboard/ with nothing but the slug returned every student: [{"rank":1,"name":"Nisha Iyer","score":5.0,"percentile":100.0}, ... {"rank":5,"name":"Meera Singh","score":0.0,"percentile":10.0}] — 10 of 10 students, full names, scores and percentiles. portal_leaderboard() checks only is_published and show_leaderboard; it never looks at share.access_mode and never requires a roll number. The toggle's helper text says "Display class rankings below each student's result", which reads as if the leaderboard only appears after a student identifies themselves.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher who deliberately chose the access-code mode to protect a class believes the link is gated. It is not: one WhatsApp forward publishes every child's name next to their mark, including the child who scored 0. For the coaching-institute owner this is the whole client roster and every competitor's ranking, harvestable in one unauthenticated GET.
findings.fix: Gate portal_leaderboard behind the same access-code check as portal_lookup (extract the check into a helper and call it from both), and require an established lookup session (e.g. issue a short-lived token from a successful lookup and require it on /leaderboard/). Force show_names off when show_leaderboard is on unless the teacher explicitly opts in, and rewrite the toggle helper text to state plainly "anyone with the link can see the full ranked list of names and scores".

findings.title: Report card, expanded results row and Student Detail each report a different set of answers for the same student
findings.route: /tests/bb3de483.../results (expand Nisha Iyer's row) vs /tests/bb3de483.../students/:id vs the report card PDF from "Download report card"
findings.observed: For Meera Singh (roll 003), the Student Detail page shows Q1 blank, Q2 A, Q3 C, Q4 C, Q5 A. Her report card PDF shows Q1 A, Q2 A, Q3 blank, Q4 C, Q5 C. Same student, same test, three of five rows disagree. Cause: report_card.py builds the table with q_num = q_pos + 1 (the printed position on that student's shuffled sheet) and takes "Correct Answer" from the sheet's answer_key, i.e. printed labels, while analytics/views.py student_detail_view emits order_index (the canonical question order) alongside the canonical question text. The expanded row on Results is a third variant, using q_pos with no question text at all (Nisha's row shows B, D, B, D, C while her detail page shows C, D, B, B, D). The report card prints no question text, so "Q3, correct answer A" cannot be resolved by the parent against anything.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the exact moment a score gets challenged. A parent brings the report card, the teacher opens Student Detail, and the two documents disagree about which question was left blank and which answer was given. There is no way to adjudicate, and the printed "correct answer" letter is meaningless because option order was shuffled per sheet. Every score in the system becomes indefensible.
findings.fix: Standardise every student-facing surface on canonical question order and canonical option labels. In report_card.py resolve q_pos through omr_sheet.question_order to the question id, number rows by the question's order_index, map the marked and correct labels back through option_order to original labels, and print the question stem (truncated) next to each row. Do the same for the expanded row in Results.jsx so all three surfaces agree.

findings.title: Rank is dense-ranked over distinct scores, so the last student in the class is shown as "#5 of 10" on screen, on the report card and on the public portal
findings.route: /tests/bb3de483.../students/:id (Meera Singh, 0/5); the same value in her report card PDF; and POST /api/v1/public/r/<slug>/lookup/
findings.observed: Scores were 5,4,4,3,3,3,3,2,2,0. Meera Singh scored 0/5, dead last of ten. Student Detail shows "RANK / PERCENTILE  #5  10th pct.  of 10 students". The report card PDF prints "Rank 5 of 10". The public portal shows a tile reading "RANK #5". percentile_rank() in psychometrics.py builds rank_map from sorted(set(scores)), so rank counts distinct score values, not students. The public leaderboard makes it self-evidently broken: ten rows numbered 1,2,2,3,3,3,3,4,4,5.
findings.why_it_hurts: Rank is the number parents and coaching-institute students care about most, and it is the one number here that is wrong in the direction that flatters. In a 40-student class with ~15 distinct scores the bottom student is told they are 15th of 40. This is printed on a document handed to a parent and served on a page the student reads unsupervised. When someone compares two report cards the deception is obvious and the product loses all credibility.
findings.fix: Use competition ranking (1,2,2,4,...) so the maximum rank equals the cohort size: rank = 1 + count of students with a strictly higher score. Keep tie handling but stop compressing the scale. If dense rank is genuinely wanted somewhere, label it separately and never render it as "#N of <cohort_size>".

findings.title: Item Analysis buckets items by printed sheet position, so it contradicts the Questions tab about which question was hardest
findings.observed: On the Questions tab the hardest question is Q4 "The chemical formula of table salt is" at 40% wrong (so p=0.60), and Q3 "Which of these is a noble gas?" is at 30% wrong (p=0.70). Switch to Item Analysis and the same test reports Q3 difficulty 0.200 and Q4 difficulty 0.500. compute_test_profile groups item_scores by resp.q_pos, but question_order differs on every sheet (verified: sheet EIBLNWEB is 260159,5a3da8,f02d78,7d0c2b,5e3b99 while 4FB3LOCY is 7d0c2b,5a3da8,260159,f02d78,5e3b99), so "item 3" is a different question for each student. The Q# column also carries no question text, so nothing signals the mismatch.
findings.why_it_hurts: "Which question do I need to reteach" is the single reason a teacher opens Analytics, and two tabs of the same page give different answers. Worse, the numbers a teacher would actually trust — discrimination, point-biserial, KR-20, and the "Questionable reliability" verdict — are all computed over these scrambled buckets, so the psychometrics are noise dressed up as rigour.
findings.fix: Resolve q_pos through omr_sheet.question_order to the question id before aggregating in compute_test_profile, key items by question id, and emit the canonical order_index plus the question stem so the Item Analysis table can show the same Q# and text as the Questions tab.

findings.title: Option distribution counts marks instead of students, so the bars contradict the wrong-rate table directly above them
findings.observed: Q4 "The chemical formula of table salt is": the Hardest questions table says 40% wrong over 10 responses (6 students correct), while the bar chart immediately below says the correct option A was chosen by 43% (3). Every question disagrees the same way. On Weekly Test 1 it is starker: Q1 shows A 50% (5), B 20% (2), C 20% (2), D 10% (1) — 10 marks from 5 students, next to a "Responses: 5" column. services.py iterates `for printed_label in resp.marked_options` and increments per label, so a sheet the reader flagged as multi-marked (one student had all four bubbles counted) inflates both the counts and the denominator. Students who left the question blank get no row at all, so Q5's bars total 9 of 10 students with nothing explaining the missing one.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher deciding whether a distractor is misleading reads "only 3 of 10 picked the right answer" and reteaches a topic the class actually got right. The percentages are of marks, not students, but are labelled as if they were students, and unresolved ambiguous sheets are silently folded in as if they were real answers, which is the exact thing the product promises never to do.
findings.fix: Count one student per question: skip responses that are flagged or multi-marked (or attribute them to an explicit "ambiguous" bucket), divide by the number of graded students rather than the number of marks, and add an explicit "No answer" row so the bars always account for every student. Add a legend stating that the green bar is the correct option.

findings.title: Results and Analytics both report "Needs review: 0" while ten sheets sit unresolved in the Review queue
findings.observed: After scanning 10 sheets, the Results header reads "10 students · Avg score: 2.9 · Needs review: 0" and the Analytics NEEDS REVIEW tile reads 0. The Review queue for the same test shows "10 items pending review" and GET /api/v1/review/?test=... returns count 10. Results.jsx computes the badge as results.filter(r => r.needs_review).length, which only sees result-level flags and is blind to sheet-level ReviewItems. Meanwhile the Weekly Test 1 rows that ARE flagged still display a hard score ("6.00/10.00" with a NEEDS REVIEW badge) and are folded into "Avg score: 4.8" with no caveat.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher's whole reason to trust this product is "uncertain reads go to a queue, never guessed". The Results page says the queue is empty when it holds every sheet in the batch, so the teacher publishes and prints report cards on unverified data. And where flags do show, the average silently includes provisional scores, so the class average moves after review with no warning that it would.
findings.fix: Have the results endpoint return the unresolved ReviewItem count for the test and render that in the Results and Analytics badges, linking straight to the queue. Gate publishing and "Download all report cards" behind a confirmation when unresolved items exist, and mark the average as provisional (e.g. "Avg 4.8, 3 sheets pending review") until the queue is empty.

findings.title: Results table has no sort, no search and no rank, and rows arrive in arbitrary order
findings.observed: The ten rows rendered in the order 006, 001, 002, 007, 005, 009, 010, 004, 008, 003 — neither roll order nor score order. No column header is clickable (zero occurrences of sort in Results.jsx), there is no search box, no rank column and no percentage column; the backend list view has no order_by at all, so the order is whatever Postgres returns and can change between loads. The only ranked view anywhere is the Analytics "Top performers" table, hard-capped at 5 rows.
findings.why_it_hurts: "Who topped and who is failing" is the first question after every test. With 40 students a teacher has to read every row twice; with 300 weekly-test students at a coaching institute it is unusable, and the ranked list they need to publish is capped at five names. Row order changing between page loads also makes it impossible to work down a list methodically.
findings.fix: Sort by score descending by default with a stable secondary sort on roll number, add sortable headers for Roll, Name and Score, add a rank column and a percentage column, and add a name/roll search box plus a "needs review only" filter. Give Top performers a "show all" that opens the full ranked list.

findings.title: Analytics is cached and never invalidated when a review item is resolved, so the public portal serves a live score beside a stale rank
findings.route: /tests/:id/review → Resolve, then /tests/:id/analytics, the report card, and /r/:slug
findings.observed: TestProfile and StudentProfile are only written by recompute_test_profile, which is triggered from omr/tasks.py when a scan batch finishes and lazily by test_profile_view when no profile exists at all. results/views.py ResolveReviewItemView recomputes the StudentResult score but contains no reference to TestProfile, StudentProfile or recompute_test_profile. The public lookup endpoint returns score straight from StudentResult but percentile and rank from the cached StudentProfile, so the two are read from different generations of the data. Nothing in the Analytics UI displays the profile's generated_at timestamp.
findings.why_it_hurts: The intended workflow is scan, fix the flagged sheets, then publish. Doing exactly that leaves KR-20, every difficulty and discrimination value, every rank and percentile, the report cards and the public portal showing pre-correction numbers with no visible staleness cue. A student who was regraded upward sees their corrected score sitting next to the rank they had before the correction.
findings.fix: Call recompute_test_profile (and re-derive StudentProfile rows) whenever a review item is resolved or a sheet is regraded. Until then, surface the profile's generated_at in the Item Analysis header and show a "recompute" action when the newest StudentResult is newer than the profile.

findings.title: Negative marking is never explained on any result surface, and blanks are rendered as wrong answers
findings.observed: negative_marks_per_wrong appears in exactly one frontend file, TestWizard.jsx, where it is configured. Grepping Results.jsx, Analytics.jsx, StudentDetail.jsx, PublicResult.jsx and report_card.py finds no mention of negative marking, marks per correct, or the marking scheme at all. Nothing on any results page states that wrong answers deduct marks or how much. On Student Detail a blank question renders with the same red ✗ as a wrong answer (Meera Singh, Q1 "blank" with a ✗), and the CSV export has a blank column but the screens do not distinguish the penalty consequence.
findings.why_it_hurts: With negative marking on, a student answering 4 of 5 correctly and one wrong does not score 4, and neither the teacher, the parent nor the student is told why. The first parent to do the arithmetic on the report card concludes the grading is broken. Showing a blank as ✗ actively teaches the wrong lesson, since under negative marking leaving it blank was the correct strategy.
findings.fix: Render the marking scheme as a one-line rule on Results, Analytics, Student Detail, the report card and the portal (e.g. "+1 per correct, 0.25 deducted per wrong, 0 for blank"). Show a distinct neutral state for blanks rather than the wrong-answer cross, and add a "marks lost to negative marking" figure to the student summary.

findings.title: A throttled public portal tells students the teacher's link is broken
findings.route: /r/:slug loaded anonymously after the shared throttle bucket is exhausted
findings.observed: The public endpoints share a ~22-30 requests/minute throttle scope keyed on IP. Once tripped, GET /api/v1/public/r/<slug>/ returns 429 and the portal renders a padlock and "Results link not available — This results link is either inactive or doesn't exist. If you received this link from your teacher, please ask them to verify it's published." I reproduced this twice: 27 meta requests from one IP put every subsequent visitor into that state. The page offers no retry, and the meta call fires twice per page load, halving the effective budget.
findings.why_it_hurts: A class of 30 students behind one school or hostel NAT opening the link at the same time will exhaust the bucket, and the app then tells all of them the teacher published it wrong. Thirty students message the teacher, the teacher republishes, nothing changes. It converts a transient rate limit into an apparent product failure at the exact moment of highest concurrency.
findings.fix: Handle 429 distinctly from 404 in PublicResult.jsx: show "Too many people are checking right now, retry in N seconds" with a countdown and auto-retry using the Retry-After header. Deduplicate the double meta fetch, give the meta endpoint a much higher (or no) throttle since it returns no student data, and key the lookup throttle on slug plus IP rather than IP alone.

findings.title: The student detail page never names the student and never shows the correct answer
findings.observed: The page title is the literal string "Student Detail" and the breadcrumb ends in "Results". Nothing on the page states which student it is — not the name, not the roll number. The per-question table has columns Q#, Question, Marked, Result: for a wrong answer it shows "C ✗" with no correct-answer column, so the teacher cannot see what the answer should have been. The student_detail_view API response confirms it: it returns score, pct, correct, wrong, blank, per_question, topic_accuracy, percentile, rank, cohort_size and no student identity at all. The RANK / PERCENTILE tile also runs its two values together with no separator, rendering as "#1100th pct." and "#510th pct."
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the screen a teacher turns toward a student or screenshares to a parent. Open two tabs and you cannot tell them apart; screenshot one and it is evidence of nothing. And the one thing the conversation is about — what the right answer was — is the one column missing, forcing a trip back to the question bank for every disputed item.
findings.fix: Add the student's name and roll to the page header and breadcrumb, and add them to the API response. Add a "Correct answer" column beside "Marked", using canonical option labels. Separate rank from percentile in the tile ("#1 of 10" over "100th percentile"). Add previous/next student navigation so a teacher can work down the class without returning to Results each time.

findings.title: Charts carry no axis titles and no value labels, so on a phone they convey no numbers at all
findings.route: /tests/:id/analytics → Overview "Score distribution" and Improvement "Class average by attempt", at 1440px and at 320px
findings.observed: The score distribution bar chart has an unlabelled y-axis (0-4, actually student count) and an unlabelled x-axis, no bar value labels, and x tick labels rotated ~45 degrees at roughly 10px. The count is only obtainable by hovering, which produces a tooltip reading "41-60% / count : 4". At 320px with isMobile there is no hover at all, so the chart is five unlabelled bars and the reader cannot recover a single number. On the Improvement tab the y-axis top label is clipped to "00%" instead of "100%", and a single-attempt test renders a full-height chart containing one unlabelled dot. The Analytics tab strip also clips "Improvement" off-screen at 320px inside a scroller with a hidden scrollbar, giving no hint the tab exists. Colours are flat solid with no gradients, which is correct.
findings.why_it_hurts: The teacher checking results on a phone between periods is the primary persona in the brief, and the headline chart is unreadable for them. Even on desktop, "how many students failed" requires hovering five bars one at a time, and a hidden fourth tab means the Improvement view is effectively undiscoverable on mobile.
findings.fix: Put the count above each bar and label the axes ("Students" and "Score band"); keep tick labels horizontal by shortening them to 0-20, 21-40 and so on. Fix the y-axis left margin so 100% is not clipped. Replace the single-attempt improvement chart with an empty state explaining that trends need at least two attempts. Give the tab strip a visible scroll affordance or wrap it at narrow widths.

findings.title: Dead "Distractor summary" section and a permanently empty Flags column on Item Analysis
findings.observed: The page renders a bold "Distractor summary" heading followed by nothing at all. The profile payload has distractor: null on every item, and DistractorSummary returns null when no item has distractor data, but Analytics.jsx renders the heading outside that guard so the orphan heading always shows once the cohort passes 10. The Flags column is likewise empty for every row even though Q3 has difficulty 0.200 and Q2 has a point-biserial of 0.112, both of which the flag vocabulary (too_hard, negative_discrimination) exists to catch. Several tabs also emit a stray "0" at the end of the page body from an unguarded && expression.
findings.why_it_hurts: The one section that would tell a teacher "option C is a dead distractor, rewrite it" is a heading over white space, and the Flags column that is supposed to do the interpreting for a non-statistician never fires, so the whole tab reduces to raw numbers the target user cannot act on.
findings.fix: Move the heading inside the DistractorSummary guard, populate item["distractor"] in compute_test_profile by calling the existing distractor_analysis(), loosen the too_hard/too_easy thresholds so a p of 0.20 flags, and replace `x.length && <X/>` with `x.length > 0 && <X/>` to stop rendering the stray 0.

findings.title: Results and Review queue headers show a raw UUID, and expanded rows number questions from zero
findings.observed: Both pages render description={`Test #${testId}`}, producing the subtitle "Test #bb3de483-40fd-4a24-a0b5-b291be2dc55f" where Analytics shows "Unit Test 3 Chemistry". At 320px that UUID wraps onto three lines and consumes a third of the header. Expanding a results row shows a table with rows labelled Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 and no question text, and the Review queue similarly identifies items as "Sheet: bb3de483-SKFZ56ER / Sheet: 075322c3-d45a-4457-941a-213ab3090316" with no student name.
findings.why_it_hurts: A teacher juggling six classes identifies a test by its name, not a 36-character UUID, and cannot confirm at a glance that they are looking at the right test before printing report cards. "Q0" is not a thing that exists on any answer sheet or in any conversation with a student.
findings.fix: Fetch the test and use its title as the page description on Results and Review (Analytics already does this). Number the expanded rows from 1 and show the question stem. Show the student name and roll on review items instead of a bare sheet UUID.

findings.title: Report card looks unfinished for a parent: em dashes, a bare percentile number, and a page and a half of "Untagged"
findings.route: "Download report card" on /tests/:id/students/:id and "Download all report cards" on /tests/:id/results
findings.observed: The generated PDF prints "Diagnostic Report — Meera Singh (003)", "No wrong answers — nothing to cluster.", "Rank unavailable — cohort too small" and the export PDF header "DoxaEd OMR — Results Report", all using em dashes, which the owner rules forbid in user-facing text; the Analytics footnote likewise uses a minus sign in "top 27% − bottom 27%". The Percentile field prints as a bare "10.0" with no "th percentile" and no explanation of what it means. Because the seeded questions carry no topics, "Topic Performance", "Topic Breakdown vs Class Average" and "Missed Items by Topic" all render a single row reading "Untagged", filling most of both pages, and the Distractor Note column is a placeholder dash. There is no test date, no class or teacher name and no signature line.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the artefact that leaves the building. As printed it reads like a debug dump: a parent sees the word "Untagged" three times, a naked "10.0", and no date telling them which test this was. It is not something a teacher would be comfortable handing over without retyping it.
findings.fix: Replace every em dash and minus sign in generated text with commas or plain wording. Render percentile as "10th percentile (of 10 students)". Collapse the topic sections to a single line, or hide them entirely, when every question is untagged, and prompt the teacher to tag questions instead. Add test date, class name and a signature line to page 1.

findings.title: Scan upload returned a raw Django debug traceback and the UI showed nothing at all, so no results could exist
findings.observed: Every scan upload failed with HTTP 500 from POST /api/v1/omr/scan/. The response body was a full Django DEBUG=True HTML traceback page ("ImportError at /api/v1/omr/scan/ — Unable to find zbar shared library"), leaking settings and file paths. In the browser the button click produced no toast, no inline error, no state change: the page still read "10 files ready" with the button enabled, indistinguishable from not having clicked. The root cause was the missing libzbar system library; I installed libzbar0 to unblock the audit, after which all 10 sheets graded correctly, so this specific cause is environmental. The silent-failure and HTML-error-page behaviours are not.
findings.why_it_hurts: Until this is fixed there are no results, no analytics and no report cards for anyone, and a teacher hitting it gets zero signal about why. They will re-click, re-upload, and conclude their photos are bad. Returning a DEBUG traceback rather than JSON also means the frontend has nothing structured to display even if it wanted to.
findings.fix: Import pyzbar at startup and fail the health check loudly if libzbar is absent, and add libzbar0 to the deployment dependencies. Ensure DRF returns JSON errors (DEBUG off in any shared environment, plus an exception handler for the scan view). In Scan.jsx surface any non-2xx as a persistent inline error with the server message and a retry, never a silent no-op.

findings.title: Public portal body is 27% of the viewport width
findings.observed: The portal's main element measures 512px inside a 1920px viewport (max-w-lg), so the result card is a narrow strip in a large empty field. The owner rule requires every page body to be 90% of available width capped at 1600px; Results and Analytics comply at 1552px, the portal does not. Content itself is clean and does not overflow at 320px.
findings.why_it_hurts: Minor on a phone where the form is the whole screen, but on the laptop a parent or office staff member uses it looks like a broken or half-loaded page, and it wastes the room needed to show a per-question breakdown or a leaderboard without scrolling.
findings.fix: Widen the portal shell to the standard 90%/1600px page shell, keeping the lookup form itself in a centred narrow column, so there is room to add the per-question breakdown and the leaderboard side by side on desktop.
